units.zh: 梁書卷第二十五 列傳第十九
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies, Number 19
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies 19

units.zh: 周捨 徐勉
units.en: Zhou She and Xu Mian
units.literal: Zhou She; Xu Mian

units.zh: 周捨字昇逸，汝南安城人，晉左光祿大夫顗之八世孫也。
units.en: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, who had served Jin as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan and an eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, the Jin Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 父顒，齊中書侍郎，有名於時。
units.en: His father Yan had been a Secretariat Attendant under Qi and was well known in his day.
units.literal: His father Yan was a Secretariat Attendant of Qi and had a reputation in his time.

units.zh: 捨幼聰潁，顒異之，臨卒謂曰：「汝不患不富貴，但當持之以道德。」
units.en: As a boy, She was quick and clever, and Yan saw something extraordinary in him. On his deathbed Yan told him, "You need not fear that you will lack wealth and rank, but you must hold yourself to moral principle."
units.literal: She in youth was clever and quick; Yan regarded him as exceptional. On his deathbed he told him, "You need not worry about lacking wealth and rank, but you must uphold yourself with moral virtue."

units.zh: 旣長，博學多通，尤精義理，善誦書，背文諷說，音韻清辯。
units.en: Once he had grown up, he was widely learned and accomplished in many subjects, especially the principles of moral reasoning. He excelled at recitation, could declaim texts from memory, and spoke with a clear voice and polished eloquence.
units.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and masterful in many fields, especially expert in principles of righteousness and reason. He was skilled at reciting books, could chant texts from memory, and his tones were clear and his eloquence refined.

units.zh: 起家齊太學博士，遷後軍行參軍。
units.en: He entered office as an Erudite of the Qi Imperial Academy and was later appointed Aide to the Rear General.
units.literal: He began his career as an Erudite of the Imperial Academy of Qi and was transferred to Aide to the Rear General.

units.zh: 建武中，魏人吳包南歸，有儒學，尚書僕射江祏招包講。
units.en: During the Jianwu reign, Wu Bao, a scholar from Wei who had come south, was invited by Vice Director Jiang Shi to give lectures on the classics.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era, the Wei man Wu Bao returned south; he had Confucian learning, and the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Jiang Shi invited Bao to lecture.

units.zh: 捨造坐，累折包，辭理遒逸，由是名爲口辯。
units.en: She took a seat in the audience and repeatedly bested Bao in debate. His arguments were forceful and elegant, and from that time he was famed for his eloquence.
units.literal: She took a seat and repeatedly refuted Bao; his reasoning was forceful and elegant, and from this he gained the name of a debater.

units.zh: 王亮爲丹陽尹，聞而悅之，辟爲主簿，政事多委焉。
units.en: When Wang Liang became Intendant of Danyang, he was delighted to hear of She and recruited him as chief clerk, delegating much of the administration to him.
units.literal: Wang Liang was Intendant of Danyang; hearing of him he was pleased and recruited him as Chief Clerk, entrusting much of the administration to him.

units.zh: 遷太常丞。
units.en: He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 梁臺建，爲奉常丞。
units.en: When the Liang regime was first set up, he was appointed Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.
units.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he became Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.

units.zh: 高祖卽位，博求異能之士。
units.en: After the High Ancestor acceded, he cast a wide net for men of exceptional talent.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he broadly sought men of unusual ability.

units.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。
units.en: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.
units.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 時天下草創，禮儀損益，多自捨出。
units.en: The empire was still being founded, and most revisions to ritual and ceremonial practice came from She.
units.literal: At that time the realm was newly founded; additions and reductions to ritual and ceremony largely came from She.

units.zh: 尋爲後軍記室參軍、秣陵令。
units.en: He was soon made Recorder on the staff of the Rear General and Magistrate of Moling.
units.literal: Soon he became Recorder of the Rear General's Staff and Magistrate of Moling.

units.zh: 入爲中書通事舍人，累遷太子洗馬，散騎常侍，中書侍郎，鴻臚卿。
units.en: He entered central government as an Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat and rose through the ranks to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
units.literal: He entered the court as Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.

units.zh: 時王亮得罪歸家，故人莫有至者，捨獨敦恩舊，及卒，身營殯葬，時人稱之。
units.en: When Wang Liang fell from favor and retired home, none of his old friends would visit him, but She alone remained loyal to their past friendship. When Wang died, She personally arranged the funeral, and people praised him for it.
units.literal: At that time Wang Liang had offended and returned home; none of his old friends came to see him, but She alone treated him with the kindness due an old associate, and when he died personally arranged the funeral; people of the time praised him.

units.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，太子右衛率，右衛將軍，雖居職屢徙，而常留省內，罕得休下。
units.en: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard. Though his titles changed often, he remained at court and seldom had a day off.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard; although his posts changed repeatedly, he constantly remained within the Secretariat and rarely had leave to go home.

units.zh: 國史詔誥，儀體法律，軍旅謀謨，皆兼掌之。
units.en: He held simultaneous responsibility for the national history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual protocol and law, and military planning.
units.literal: National history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual forms and laws, and military strategy and counsel—he held charge of them all.

units.zh: 日夜侍上，預機密，二十餘年未嘗離左右。
units.en: Day and night he attended the emperor and shared in state secrets; for more than twenty years he was never far from his side.
units.literal: Day and night he attended the sovereign and took part in confidential affairs; for more than twenty years he never left his side.

units.zh: 捨素辯給，與人泛論談謔，終日不絕口，而竟無一言漏泄機事，衆尤嘆服之。
units.en: She was naturally quick-witted and loved to debate and banter with others, talking without pause all day long, yet he never let a single secret slip. People admired him all the more for it.
units.literal: She was by nature quick in debate; with others he would discourse broadly and jest, talking without cease all day, yet in the end not a single word of confidential affairs leaked out, and the multitude especially admired and submitted to this.

units.zh: 性儉素，衣服器用，居處床席，如布衣之貧者。
units.en: He lived plainly by nature: his clothes, furnishings, room, bed, and bedding were no better than a poor commoner's.
units.literal: By nature he was frugal and plain; his clothes, implements, dwelling, bed, and mat were like those of a poor commoner.

units.zh: 每入官府，雖廣廈華堂，閨閤重邃，捨居之則塵埃滿積。
units.en: Wherever he lodged in government offices, however grand the halls and chambers, his rooms were left thick with dust.
units.literal: Whenever he entered an official residence, though it had broad halls and splendid chambers with inner apartments deep and secluded, where She dwelt dust would pile up thick.

units.zh: 以荻爲鄣，壞亦不營。
units.en: He used reed mats for partitions and did not bother to replace them when they wore out.
units.literal: He used reeds for screens; when they broke he did not repair them.

units.zh: 爲右衛，母憂去職，起爲明威將軍、右驍騎將軍。
units.en: While he was General of the Right Guard, he left office to observe mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended, he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.
units.literal: While serving as Right Guard, he left office on his mother's death; on mourning's end he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.

units.zh: 服闋，除侍中，領步兵校尉，未拜，仍遷員外散騎常侍、太子左衛率。
units.en: After mourning he was named Palace Attendant and concurrent Colonel of the Footsoldiers, but before he could assume those posts he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
units.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers; before he could take up the appointment he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

units.zh: 頃之，加散騎常侍、本州大中正，遷太子詹事。
units.en: Soon afterward he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of his home province, and was promoted to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
units.literal: Shortly thereafter he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of his native province, and was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

units.zh: 普通五年，南津獲武陵太守白渦書，許遺捨面錢百萬，津司以聞。
units.en: In the fifth year of Putong, officials at South Ford seized a letter from Bai Wo, Administrator of Wuling, promising to pay She a million cash in person, and reported the matter.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, at South Ford a letter from Bai Wo, Administrator of Wuling, was seized, promising to give She a million in cash face to face; the ford office reported it.

units.zh: 雖書自外入，猶爲有司所奏，捨坐免。
units.en: Even though the letter had come from outside, the authorities still impeached him, and She was dismissed from office.
units.literal: Although the letter came from outside, he was still impeached by the responsible officials, and She was punished by dismissal.

units.zh: 遷右驍騎將軍，知太子詹事。
units.en: He was reappointed General of the Right Swift Cavalry and served concurrently as acting Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
units.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Swift Cavalry and acted as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

units.zh: 以其年卒，時年五十六。
units.en: He died later that year, at the age of fifty-six.
units.literal: In that same year he died, at the age of fifty-six.

units.zh: 上臨哭，哀慟左右。
units.en: The emperor came in person to mourn him, and his grief moved everyone around him.
units.literal: The sovereign came in person to mourn; his grief moved those on his left and right.

units.zh: 詔曰：「太子詹事、豫州大中正捨，奄至殞喪，惻愴于懷。
units.en: An edict read: "Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou, She, has died suddenly, and my heart is full of grief.
units.literal: An edict said: "Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou She has suddenly met with death; my heart is pierced with sorrow.

units.zh: 其學思堅明，志行開敏，劬勞機要，多歷歲年，才用未窮，彌可嗟慟。
units.en: His learning was solid and his mind clear, his character open and his conduct sharp. He labored at the heart of government for many years, and his talents were far from spent—how deeply this grieves me.
units.literal: His learning and thought were firm and clear, his will and conduct open and keen; he toiled at crucial affairs through many years, his talent and use not yet exhausted—how much the more lamentable.

units.zh: 宜隆追遠，以旌善人。
units.en: Let us honor the dead and thereby commend a man of virtue.
units.literal: It is fitting to elevate remembrance of the distant and thereby honor a good man.

units.zh: 可贈侍中、護軍將軍，鼓吹一部，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事隨由資給。
units.en: Let him be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, with one band of ceremonial music, the secret funerary vessels from the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and whatever funds the funeral requires.
units.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, one set of ceremonial music, the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and funeral expenses supplied as needed.

units.zh: 諡曰簡子。」
units.en: His posthumous title was Jianzi, 'the Plain.'"
units.literal: His posthumous title was Jianzi."

units.zh: 明年，又詔曰：「故侍中、護軍將軍簡子捨，義該玄儒，博窮文史，奉親能孝，事君盡忠，歷掌機密，清貞自居。
units.en: The following year another edict read: "The late Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, Jianzi She, embodied the deepest Confucian learning and mastered literature and history. He was filial to his parents and wholly loyal to his sovereign. He held confidential posts for years and lived in unstained integrity.
units.literal: The next year, another edict said: "The late Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, Jianzi She, embraced the meaning of the profound Ruists and exhaustively mastered literature and history; in serving his parents he could be filial, in serving his lord he was wholly loyal; through successive terms he held confidential affairs and kept himself pure and upright.

units.zh: 食不重味，身靡兼衣。
units.en: He never ate two dishes of the same kind at one meal, and never wore more than one layer of clothing at a time.
units.literal: In food he did not repeat flavors; on his person he did not wear layered garments.

units.zh: 終亡之日，內無妻妾，外無田宅，兩兒單貧，有過古烈。
units.en: When he died he had no wife or concubine at home and no fields or house abroad. His two sons were left alone in poverty, and his austerity surpassed that of the stern worthies of old.
units.literal: On the day of his final death he had no wife or concubine within, no fields or residence without; his two sons were alone and poor—he surpassed the stern worthies of antiquity.

units.zh: 往者，南司白渦之劾，恐外議謂朕有私，致此黜免，追愧若人一介之善。
units.en: When the southern office impeached him over Bai Wo, I feared people would think I acted from private motives and allowed his dismissal. Looking back, I regret having lost even one man's small measure of goodness.
units.literal: Formerly, in the impeachment by the southern office concerning Bai Wo, I feared outside opinion would say I had private motives and so caused this dismissal; looking back, I regret losing even one man's small measure of goodness.

units.zh: 外可量加褒異，以旌善人。」
units.en: Let additional honors be granted as befits the case, to commend a man of virtue."
units.literal: Externally he may be given additional honors according to measure, to commend a good man."

units.zh: 二子：弘義，弘信。
units.en: He had two sons: Hongyi and Hongxin.
units.literal: He had two sons: Hongyi and Hongxin.

units.zh: 徐勉字脩仁，東海郯人也。
units.en: Xu Mian, whose courtesy name was Xiuren, came from Tan in Donghai.
units.literal: Xu Mian, styled Xiuren, was a native of Tan in Donghai.

units.zh: 祖長宗，宋高祖霸府行參軍。
units.en: His grandfather Changzong had served the Song founder as Aide on the staff of his headquarters.
units.literal: His grandfather Changzong was Acting Aide of the Song High Ancestor's hegemonial headquarters.

units.zh: 父融，南昌相。
units.en: His father Rong had been Chancellor of Nanchang.
units.literal: His father Rong was Chancellor of Nanchang.

units.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。
units.en: Mian lost his father young and grew up poor, but from an early age he cultivated a life of integrity.
units.literal: Mian in youth was orphaned and poor and early cultivated pure integrity.

units.zh: 年六歲，時屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾爲文，見稱耆宿。
units.en: At the age of six, during a long spell of rain, his family prayed for clear weather. He spontaneously composed a piece of writing and was praised by the elders.
units.literal: At age six, when there was prolonged rain, the family prayed for clear skies; he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.

units.zh: 及長，篤志好學。
units.en: As he grew older, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to study.
units.literal: When he grew up, he was steadfast in will and fond of learning.

units.zh: 起家國子生。
units.en: He entered official life as a student of the Imperial University.
units.literal: He began his career as a student of the Imperial University.

units.zh: 太尉文憲公王儉時爲祭酒，每稱勉有宰輔之量。
units.en: Wang Jian, Duke Wenxian and Grand Marshal, was then Libationer of the university and often said that Mian had the makings of a chief minister.
units.literal: The Grand Marshal, Duke Wenxian Wang Jian, was then Libationer, and often said Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.

units.zh: 射策舉高第，補西陽王國侍郎。
units.en: He placed at the top of the archery-and-policy examination and was appointed Attendant to the Prince of Xiyang.
units.literal: In the target-and-plan examination he achieved a high grade and was appointed Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiyang.

units.zh: 尋遷太學博士，鎮軍參軍，尚書殿中郎，以公事免。
units.en: He was soon promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat, but was later dismissed over an official matter.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat; he was dismissed on account of official business.

units.zh: 又除中兵郎、領軍長史。
units.en: He was later appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk on the staff of the Army Guard.
units.literal: He was again appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk of the Army Guard.

units.zh: 琅邪王元長才名甚盛，嘗欲與勉相識，每託人召之。
units.en: Wang Yuanchang, Prince of Langye, was then at the height of his fame, and he repeatedly tried to arrange a meeting with Mian through intermediaries.
units.literal: The Prince of Langye Wang Yuanchang had a very flourishing reputation for talent; he once wished to become acquainted with Mian and repeatedly had others summon him.

units.zh: 勉謂人曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕醿衣裾。」
units.en: Mian told an acquaintance, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short-lived. One should not lightly trail in his wake."
units.literal: Mian told someone, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly wet the hem of one's robe with him."

units.zh: 俄而元長及禍，時人莫不服其機鑒。
units.en: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and everyone marveled at Mian's foresight.
units.literal: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and people of the time all submitted to his keen foresight.

units.zh: 初與長沙宣武王游，高祖深器賞之。
units.en: Early on he became close to Xiao Yi, King of Changsha and King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor came to think highly of him.
units.literal: Early on he associated with the King of Changsha, King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor deeply valued and appreciated him.

units.zh: 及義兵至京邑，勉於新林謁見，高祖甚加恩禮，使管書記。
units.en: When the righteous army reached the capital, Mian presented himself at Xinlin. The High Ancestor treated him with special favor and put him in charge of records and correspondence.
units.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital region, Mian presented himself at Xinlin; the High Ancestor greatly added favor and ceremony and had him manage documents and records.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜中書侍郎，遷建威將軍、後軍諮議參軍、本邑中正、尚書左丞。
units.en: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Mian was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and soon promoted to General Who Establishes Might, advisory staff officer to the Rear Army, rectifier of his home district, and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant and transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear Army, Rectifier of his native district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 自掌樞憲，多所糾舉，時論以爲稱職。
units.en: Once he held authority over legal discipline, he brought many cases to account, and public opinion held that he was thoroughly fit for the post.
units.literal: From the time he held the pivot of law and discipline, he impeached many cases; opinion of the time held that he was fit for his post.

units.zh: 天監二年，除給事黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。
units.en: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, sharing responsibility for major appointments.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, participating in the great selection.

units.zh: 遷侍中。
units.en: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.
units.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 時王師北伐，候驛填委。
units.en: At that time the imperial army was campaigning in the north, and courier stations were buried under dispatches.
units.literal: At that time the royal army marched north; courier stations were piled with dispatches.

units.zh: 勉參掌軍書，劬勞夙夜，動經數旬，乃一還宅。
units.en: Mian shared responsibility for military correspondence and labored day and night. Weeks would pass before he returned home even once.
units.literal: Mian participated in managing military documents, toiling from early to late; often several tens of days would pass before he returned home once.

units.zh: 每還，羣犬驚吠。
units.en: Whenever he did return, the household dogs barked in alarm at the stranger.
units.literal: Whenever he returned, the pack of dogs would bark in alarm.

units.zh: 勉歎曰：「吾憂國忘家，乃至於此。
units.en: Mian sighed and said, "I have worried for the state until I have forgotten my own home—even to this point.
units.literal: Mian sighed and said, "I worry for the state and forget my home, even to this point.

units.zh: 若吾亡後，亦是傳中一事。」
units.en: When I am gone, this too will be a story worth telling."
units.literal: After my death, this too will be an incident recorded in my biography."

units.zh: 六年，除給事中、五兵尚書，遷吏部尚書。
units.en: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and was then promoted to Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 勉居選官，彝倫有序，旣閑尺牘，兼善辭令，雖文案填積，坐客充滿，應對如流，手不停筆。
units.en: As head of personnel appointments, Mian kept the hierarchy in good order. He was adept at paperwork and equally skilled at formal speech. Though documents piled up and his hall was always full of visitors, he answered with effortless fluency while his brush never stopped moving.
units.literal: Mian held the post of selection officer; human relations were in order. He was already skilled in documents and also good at formal addresses. Though papers piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water and his hand did not stop the brush.

units.zh: 又該綜百氏，皆爲避諱。
units.en: He also possessed comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and took care to avoid all their taboo names.
units.literal: He also had comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and avoided the taboo names of them all.

units.zh: 常及閘入夜集，客有虞皓求詹事五官，勉正色答云：「今夕止可談風月，不宜及公事。」
units.en: He often entertained guests late into the night after the gates had closed. Once a guest named Yu Hao asked him about an appointment as one of the Five Officials under the Grand Tutor. Mian answered sternly, "Tonight we may speak only of poetry and the moon. Official business is out of place."
units.literal: He often gathered guests after the gate closing into the night; a guest, Yu Hao, sought the Five Officials post under the Grand Tutor. Mian with stern countenance replied, "This evening we may only discuss wind and moon; it is not fitting to touch official business."

units.zh: 故時人咸服其無私。
units.en: People admired him all the more for his impartiality.
units.literal: Therefore people of the time all submitted to his lack of private interest.

units.zh: 除散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍，未拜，改領太子右衛率。
units.en: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrent General of Roaming Attack, but before he could assume the post he was reassigned as Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
units.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently General of Roaming Attack; before taking up the appointment he was changed to concurrent Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

units.zh: 遷左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。
units.en: He was promoted to General of the Left Guard and concurrent Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, attending the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事。
units.en: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young, and Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs on his behalf.
units.literal: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young; he was ordered to manage palace affairs.

units.zh: 太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。
units.en: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and consulted him on every matter.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and on every matter sought his counsel.

units.zh: 嘗於殿內講《孝經》，臨川靖惠王、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充爲執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕爲侍講。
units.en: Once, in the palace hall, he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety." The King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer Zhang Chong held the text; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.
units.literal: Once within the hall he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety"; the King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.

units.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡時譽，勉陳讓數四。
units.en: The men chosen were the most eminent kinsmen and worthies of the day, and Mian declined the honor four times.
units.literal: The selection at the time reached the utmost in kinship and worth, wonderfully exhausting the reputation of the age; Mian submitted declining statements four times.

units.zh: 又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔不許，然後就焉。
units.en: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to take the lesser role of lecturing attendant instead, but the emperor refused, and only then did he accept the appointment.
units.literal: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to exchange for the post of lecturing attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.

units.zh: 轉太子詹事，領雲騎將軍，尋加散騎常侍，遷尚書右僕射，詹事如故。
units.en: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent General of Cloud Cavalry, soon given the additional title of Regular Attendant, and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Cloud Cavalry; soon he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Tutor as before.

units.zh: 又改授侍中，頻表解宮職，優詔不許。
units.en: He was later appointed Palace Attendant and repeatedly petitioned to resign, but the emperor's gracious edicts refused each request.
units.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant; he repeatedly submitted memorials resigning office, but gracious edicts did not permit it.

units.zh: 時人間喪事，多不遵禮，朝終夕殯，相尚以速。
units.en: At that time many people ignored proper funeral rites, encoffining the dead the same evening they died and competing to see who could bury fastest.
units.literal: At that time in people's funerals many did not follow ritual; mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, and they vied with one another in speed.

units.zh: 勉上疏曰：「《禮記問喪》云：『三日而後斂者，以俟其生也。
units.en: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "In the Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' it says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to wait in case the person may yet live.
units.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "The Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to await the person's return to life.

units.zh: 三日而不生，亦不生矣。』
units.en: If after three days he has not revived, he will not revive.'
units.literal: If after three days he does not live, he will not live.

units.zh: 自頃以來，不遵斯制。
units.en: In recent times this rule has been ignored.
units.literal: From recent times onward, this regulation has not been followed.

units.zh: 送終之禮，殯以期日，潤屋豪家，乃或半晷，衣衾棺槨，以速爲榮，親戚徒隸，各念休反。
units.en: Funerals are now scheduled for a fixed day, and in wealthy households the encoffining sometimes takes only half a day. Fine shrouds and coffins are prized for how quickly they can be finished. Relatives, servants, and retainers all think only of getting back to their rest.
units.literal: In the rites of seeing one off at the end, encoffining is set for a fixed day; wealthy households sometimes do it in half a day. Garments, covers, coffin, and outer coffin—taking speed as glory; kin, servants, and retainers each think of rest and return.

units.zh: 故屬纊才畢，灰釘已具，忘狐鼠之顧步，愧燕雀之徊翔。
units.en: As soon as the final breath is taken, the lime and nails are already ready. They forget how even foxes and rats pause over the dead, and they would be shamed by the swallows and sparrows that hover and hesitate.
units.literal: Thus as soon as the last breath is placed, lime and nails are already prepared; they forget the fox and rat's lingering steps and are ashamed before the swallows and sparrows' hovering flight.

units.zh: 傷情滅理，莫此爲大。
units.en: Nothing does more violence to human feeling and moral principle than this.
units.literal: To wound feeling and extinguish principle—nothing is greater than this.

units.zh: 且人子承衾之時，志懣心絕，喪事所資，悉關他手，愛憎深淺，事實難原。
units.en: Moreover, when a son receives the death shroud, his heart is broken with grief. Everything needed for the funeral is handled by others, and it is hard to know whether their actions spring from love or from indifference.
units.literal: Moreover, when a son receives the coverlet, his will is aggrieved and his heart cut off; what the funeral relies on is entirely in others' hands—the depth of love or hate is in fact hard to trace to its source.

units.zh: 如覘視或爽，存沒違濫，使萬有其一，怨酷已多。
units.en: If the watching of the body is neglected or the rites for the living and the dead are confused, even if only one case in ten thousand goes wrong, the grief and injustice will be great.
units.literal: If observation or attendance is neglected, and the living and dead are violated and confused, even if only one in ten thousand suffers this, the grievance and cruelty are already many.

units.zh: 豈若緩其告斂之晨，申其望生之冀。
units.en: How much better to delay the morning of encoffinement and preserve the hope that life may yet return?
units.literal: How does this compare with slowing the morning of announcing encoffinement and extending the hope of return to life?

units.zh: 請自今士庶，宜悉依古，三日大斂。
units.en: I ask that from now on gentlemen and commoners alike follow the ancient practice and wait three days before encoffining the body.
units.literal: I request that from now on gentry and commoners should all follow the ancients and perform great encoffinement after three days.

units.zh: 如有不奉，加以糾繩。」
units.en: Those who fail to comply should be subject to investigation and punishment."
units.literal: If there are those who do not comply, let correction and punishment be applied."

units.zh: 詔可其奏。
units.en: The emperor approved his memorial.
units.literal: An edict approved his memorial.

units.zh: 尋授宣惠將軍，置佐史，侍中、僕射如故。
units.en: He was soon appointed General Who Proclaims Favor with a full staff, while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Vice Director.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Proclaims Favor, with staff officers established; Palace Attendant and Vice Director as before.

units.zh: 又除尚書僕射、中衛將軍。
units.en: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.
units.literal: He was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.

units.zh: 勉以舊恩，越升重位，盡心奉上，知無不爲。
units.en: Because of his long service, Mian was promoted beyond the usual measure to high office. He devoted himself wholly to the throne and left nothing undone.
units.literal: Mian, by reason of old favor, was promoted beyond his rank to a heavy post; he devoted his heart in serving above and there was nothing he knew that he did not do.

units.zh: 爰自小選，迄於此職，常參掌衡石，甚得士心。
units.en: From his early work in personnel selection to this highest post, he had long held the scales of appointment, and he won the deep respect of the scholarly class.
units.literal: From the time of minor selection until this post, he constantly participated in holding the balance and stone, and greatly won the hearts of scholars.

units.zh: 禁省中事，未嘗漏泄。
units.en: He never disclosed a single matter from within the palace offices.
units.literal: Matters within the forbidden precincts, he never leaked.

units.zh: 每有表奏，輒焚藳草。
units.en: Whenever he drafted a memorial, he burned the working copy afterward.
units.literal: Whenever he had memorials submitted, he always burned the draft manuscripts.

units.zh: 博通經史，多識前載。
units.en: He was deeply learned in the classics and histories and knew a great deal of earlier historical writing.
units.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and knew much of earlier records.

units.zh: 朝儀國典，婚冠吉凶，勉皆預圖議。
units.en: Mian took part in drafting and deliberating on court ritual, state institutions, marriage and capping ceremonies, and rites of mourning and celebration.
units.literal: Court ceremonies, state institutions, marriage and capping, auspicious and inauspicious rites — Mian all participated in planning and discussion.

units.zh: 普通六年，上修五禮表曰：
units.en: In the sixth year of the Putong era, Mian submitted a memorial on the revision of the Five Rites, which read:
units.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, he submitted a memorial on revising the Five Rites, saying:

units.zh: 臣聞「立天之道，曰陰與陽；
units.en: Your subject has heard it said: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to set forth yin and yang;
units.literal: Your subject has heard: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to name yin and yang;

units.zh: 立人之道，曰仁與義。」
units.en: and to establish the Way of Humanity is to set forth benevolence and righteousness."
units.literal: to establish the Way of Humanity is to name benevolence and righteousness."

units.zh: 故稱「導之以德，齊之以禮」。
units.en: Hence the saying: "Lead the people with virtue, and harmonize them with ritual."
units.literal: Therefore it is said: "Guide them with virtue, regulate them with ritual."

units.zh: 夫禮所以安上治民，弘風訓俗，經國家，利後嗣者也。
units.en: Ritual is what steadies those above, governs the people, shapes custom, educates society, sustains the state, and brings benefit to future generations.
units.literal: Now ritual is what settles superiors, governs the people, spreads custom, instructs society, orders the state, and benefits posterity.

units.zh: 唐虞三代，咸必由之。
units.en: The eras of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties all relied upon it without exception.
units.literal: Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all necessarily followed it.

units.zh: 在乎有周，憲章尤備，因殷革夏，損益可知。
units.en: Under the Zhou, the constitutional order was especially complete; inheriting from Yin and reforming Xia, its additions and revisions can still be traced.
units.literal: In the Zhou era, constitutional models were especially complete; building on Yin and reforming Xia, additions and subtractions can be known.

units.zh: 雖復經禮三百，曲禮三千，經文三百，威儀三千，其大歸有五，卽宗伯所掌典禮：吉爲上，凶次之，賓次之，軍次之，嘉爲下也。
units.en: Though tradition speaks of three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical passages, and three thousand rules of deportment, the great divisions are five — the ritual canon overseen by the Minister of Rites: auspicious rites first, inauspicious rites second, guest rites third, military rites fourth, and celebratory rites last.
units.literal: Although there were again three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical texts, and three thousand rules of bearing, their great categories number five — namely the canonical rites administered by the Minister of Rites: auspicious rites rank first, inauspicious rites next, guest rites next, military rites next, and celebratory rites last.

units.zh: 故祠祭不以禮，則不齊不莊；
units.en: If sacrifice is not performed according to ritual, worship becomes disorderly and undignified;
units.literal: Therefore if sacrificial offerings are not conducted according to ritual, then there is neither order nor dignity;

units.zh: 喪紀不以禮，則背死忘生者衆；
units.en: if mourning is not governed by ritual, many will abandon the dead and neglect the living;
units.literal: if mourning regulations are not according to ritual, then those who turn their backs on the dead and forget the living are many;

units.zh: 賓客不以禮，則朝覲失其儀；
units.en: if the reception of guests is not regulated by ritual, audiences at court lose their proper order;
units.literal: if guests are not treated according to ritual, then court audiences lose their proper form;

units.zh: 軍旅不以禮，則致亂于師律；
units.en: if armies are not governed by ritual, military discipline falls into chaos;
units.literal: if armies are not governed according to ritual, then disorder is brought into military discipline;

units.zh: 冠婚不以禮，則男女失其時。
units.en: if capping and marriage are not conducted according to ritual, men and women miss the proper seasons of life.
units.literal: if capping and marriage are not according to ritual, then men and women miss their proper seasons.

units.zh: 爲國修身，於斯攸急。
units.en: For ordering the state and cultivating the self, nothing is more urgent than this.
units.literal: For governing the state and cultivating the person, in this matter it is most urgent.

units.zh: 洎周室大壞，王道旣衰，官守斯文，日失其序。
units.en: When the Zhou house collapsed and the royal way declined, the officials charged with preserving these traditions lost their proper order day by day.
units.literal: When the Zhou house was greatly ruined and the royal way had already declined, officials who guarded this culture daily lost its order.

units.zh: 禮樂征伐，出自諸侯，《小雅》盡廢，舊章缺矣。
units.en: Ritual, music, war, and punishment passed from the throne to the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" fell wholly into disuse, and the old regulations were lost.
units.literal: Ritual, music, campaigns, and punishments issued from the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" were entirely abandoned, and old statutes were lost.

units.zh: 是以韓宣適魯，知周公之德；
units.en: Thus when Han Xuan of Jin visited Lu, he came to understand the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;
units.literal: Therefore when Han Xuan went to Lu, he knew the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;

units.zh: 叔侯在晉，辨郊勞之儀。
units.en: and Shu Hou, serving in Jin, was able to explain the rites of suburban welcome.
units.literal: Shu Hou was in Jin and distinguished the rites of suburban welcome.

units.zh: 戰國從橫，政教愈泯；
units.en: In the Warring States period of shifting alliances, government and moral instruction sank ever deeper into obscurity;
units.literal: In the Warring States era of vertical and horizontal alliances, government and teaching grew ever more extinguished;

units.zh: 暴秦滅學，掃地無餘。
units.en: Then tyrannical Qin suppressed learning and swept the ground bare, leaving nothing behind.
units.literal: Violent Qin destroyed learning, sweeping the ground and leaving nothing.

units.zh: 漢氏鬱興，日不暇給，猶命叔孫于外野，方知帝王之爲貴。
units.en: When the Han rose in splendor, its affairs were so pressing that each day left no spare moment; yet the court still had to summon Shusun Tong from the wilderness to devise rites, and only then did men understand how precious imperial dignity truly was.
units.literal: The Han dynasty flourished abundantly, with days not enough to supply its needs; still it ordered Shusun in the outer wilds, and only then knew how precious being emperor and king was.

units.zh: 末葉紛綸，遞有興毀，或以武功銳志，或好黃老之言，禮義之式，於焉中止。
units.en: In the later generations of Han, affairs grew ever more tangled, with one dynasty rising as another fell; some rulers pursued military glory with single-minded zeal, others favored the teachings of Huang-Lao — and the forms of ritual and righteousness came to a halt.
units.literal: In the late branches, affairs were tangled, successively rising and falling; some were sharp in military achievement, some favored the words of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi — the forms of ritual and righteousness thereupon ceased.

units.zh: 及東京曹褒，南宮制述，集其散略，百有餘篇，雖寫以尺簡，而終闕平奏。
units.en: At the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao compiled ritual texts at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered materials into more than a hundred chapters; though copied onto bamboo slips, the work was never brought to completion and formally submitted.
units.literal: By the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao formulated and compiled at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered outlines into more than a hundred pieces; though written on foot-long slips, in the end they lacked completion and submission.

units.zh: 其後兵革相尋，異端互起，章句旣淪，俎豆斯輟。
units.en: After that, war followed upon war, heterodox teachings multiplied, classical commentaries sank into oblivion, and sacrificial vessels fell silent.
units.literal: Afterward warfare followed in succession, heterodox teachings rose one after another, commentarial passages sank away, and sacrificial vessels ceased.

units.zh: 方領矩步之容，事滅於旌鼓；
units.en: The dignified bearing of square collars and measured steps vanished in the clash of banners and drums;
units.literal: The bearing of square collars and measured steps perished amid banners and drums;

units.zh: 蘭臺石室之文，用盡於帷蓋。
units.en: and the texts preserved in the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were consumed to make tent covers.
units.literal: The texts of the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were entirely used up as tent coverings.

units.zh: 至乎晉初，爰定新禮，荀顗制之於前，摯虞刪之於末。
units.en: At the beginning of Jin, a new ritual code was established: Xun Yi drafted it at the outset, and Zhi Yu revised it at the end.
units.literal: Reaching the beginning of Jin, then the new rites were fixed — Xun Yi formulated them at the start, Zhi Yu edited them at the end.

units.zh: 旣而中原喪亂，罕有所遺；
units.en: But when the Central Plains were overrun by chaos, little of it survived;
units.literal: Soon the Central Plains fell into disorder, and little was left behind;

units.zh: 江左草創，因循而已。
units.en: in the southeast the dynasty was newly founded, and men could do no more than follow old precedent.
units.literal: In the southeast, it was newly established, and they merely followed precedent.

units.zh: 𨤸革之風，是則未暇。
units.en: As for the spirit of reform and innovation, there was no time for it at all.
units.literal: The winds of reform and innovation — for that they had no leisure.

units.zh: 伏惟陛下睿明啓運，先天改物，撥亂惟武，經世以文。
units.en: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and discerning, has inaugurated a new age, transformed the realm in accord with Heaven's mandate, quelled disorder through martial power, and governed the world through culture.
units.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and bright, inaugurated the destiny, changed things before Heaven, quelled disorder through martial virtue, and ordered the age through culture.

units.zh: 作樂在乎功成，制禮弘於業定。
units.en: Music is made when merit is achieved; ritual is established in full when the great enterprise is secure.
units.literal: Making music lies in accomplishing merit; instituting ritual is magnified when the enterprise is settled.

units.zh: 光啓二學，皇枝等於貴遊；
units.en: You opened two imperial academies, placing imperial clansmen on equal footing with the sons of the nobility;
units.literal: You opened two academies, placing imperial branches on a par with noble scions;

units.zh: 辟茲五館，草萊升以好爵。
units.en: and established these five halls of learning, so that men from humble fields might rise to honorable office.
units.literal: You established these five halls, so men from humble fields rose to fine rank.

units.zh: 爰自受命，迄于告成，盛德形容備矣，天下能事畢矣。
units.en: From the moment you received the mandate until the present completion of your work, your great virtue has been fully realized, and every task the realm could undertake has been accomplished.
units.literal: From accepting the mandate until announcing completion, your abundant virtue has been fully described, and all the world could do is done.

units.zh: 明明穆穆，無德而稱焉。
units.en: Bright in wisdom and dignified in bearing, your virtue exceeds what any words can adequately praise.
units.literal: Bright and dignified, there are no words adequate to praise your virtue.

units.zh: 至若玄符靈貺之祥，浮溟機山之賮，固亦日書左史，副在司存，今可得而略也。
units.en: As for the auspicious signs of mystical talismans and divine blessings, and the tribute brought from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are recorded daily by the court scribes and preserved in the archives; they may be passed over briefly here.
units.literal: As for auspicious signs of mysterious talismans and spiritual blessings, tribute from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are daily recorded by the left scribe and duplicated in the keeping offices; now they may be briefly noted.

units.zh: 是以命彼羣才，搜甘泉之法；
units.en: Therefore Your Majesty summoned many men of talent to search out the ritual precedents of Ganquan;
units.literal: Therefore you ordered those many talents to search out the methods of Ganquan;

units.zh: 延茲碩學，闡曲臺之儀。
units.en: and invited eminent scholars to expound the rites compiled at the Qutai Platform.
units.literal: and invited these eminent scholars to expound the rites of Qutai Platform.

units.zh: 淄上淹中之儒，連蹤繼軌；
units.en: Confucian scholars from Linzi and the Yanzhong academy came in an unbroken stream;
units.literal: Confucian scholars of Zi River and Yanzhong followed one after another on the same path;

units.zh: 負笈懷鈆之彥，匪旦伊夕。
units.en: and learned men bearing book-chests and writing tablets arrived not in a day or a night alone.
units.literal: Men of talent bearing book-chests and carrying writing styli came not merely overnight.

units.zh: 諒以化穆三雍，人從五典，秩宗之教，勃焉以興。
units.en: Surely through the civilizing influence of the Three Yong academies, the people were brought into accord with the Five Classics, and the teachings overseen by the Minister of Rites vigorously revived.
units.literal: Surely through transforming the Three Yong, people followed the Five Classics — the teachings of the Minister of Rites vigorously arose.

units.zh: 伏尋所定五禮，起齊永明三年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表求制一代禮樂，于時參議置新舊學士十人，止修五禮，諮稟衛將軍丹陽尹王儉，學士亦分住郡中，製作歷年，猶未克就。
units.en: I humbly review the history of the Five Rites now completed: the project began in the third year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Infantry Commandant to the Crown Prince, submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for the age. At that time the court deliberated appointing ten senior and junior academicians to work exclusively on the Five Rites, reporting to Wang Jian, General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang. The academicians were also dispersed to various commanderies. Years of work passed, yet the project remained unfinished.
units.literal: I humbly examine the fixed Five Rites: they began in the third year of Yongming of Qi, when the Crown Prince's Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for one generation. At that time it was deliberated to appoint ten old and new academicians, restricting the work to the Five Rites, with consultation and reporting to General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang Wang Jian. The academicians also dispersed to reside in various commanderies. Production continued for years, yet it was still not completed.

units.zh: 及文憲薨殂，遺文散逸，後又以事付國子祭酒何胤，經涉九載，猶復未畢。
units.en: When Wang Jian, posthumously titled Wen Xian, died, his surviving manuscripts were scattered and lost. The task was later entrusted to He Yin, Director of the Imperial Academy; nine more years passed, and the work was still incomplete.
units.literal: When Wen Xian died, his surviving texts were scattered and lost. Later the task was again entrusted to Director of the Imperial Academy He Yin; nine years passed, and still it was not finished.

units.zh: 建武四年，胤還東山，齊明帝敕委尚書令徐孝嗣。
units.en: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin retired to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the project be entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the matter be entrusted to Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi.

units.zh: 舊事本末，隨在南第。
units.en: The original materials, with their full history, were kept at his Southern Residence.
units.literal: The beginning and end of the old affair followed him to the Southern Residence.

units.zh: 永元中，孝嗣於此遇禍，又多零落。
units.en: During the Yongyuan era, Xu Xiaosi met with disaster there, and much of the material was again lost.
units.literal: In the Yongyuan era, Xiaosi met calamity there, and much was again scattered and lost.

units.zh: 當時鳩斂所餘，權付尚書左丞蔡仲熊、驍騎將軍何佟之，共掌其事。
units.en: What remained from the earlier collection was provisionally entrusted to Cai Zhongxiong, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and He Tongzhi, General of Valiant Cavalry, who jointly oversaw the work.
units.literal: What remained from the collection at that time was provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi, who jointly managed the affair.

units.zh: 時修禮局住在國子學中門外，東昏之代，頻有軍火，其所散失，又逾太半。
units.en: The ritual revision bureau was then housed outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. During the reign of Emperor Hun, repeated military fires broke out, and more than half of what remained was again lost.
units.literal: At that time the ritual revision bureau was located outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. In the reign of Emperor Hun, there were repeated military fires; what was scattered and lost again exceeded more than half.

units.zh: 天監元年，佟之啓審省置之宜，敕使外詳。
units.en: In the first year of Tianjian, He Tongzhi submitted a memorial on whether the bureau should be retained or abolished, and an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate the matter.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, Tongzhi submitted a memorial examining whether it was appropriate to reduce or retain the bureau; an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate in detail.

units.zh: 時尚書參詳，以天地初革，庶務權輿，宜俟隆平，徐議刪撰。
units.en: The Secretariat then deliberated and concluded that, with the realm newly transformed and every branch of government still in its infancy, it would be best to wait until peace was fully established before proceeding with revision and compilation.
units.literal: At that time the Secretariat deliberated in detail, holding that Heaven and Earth had just been transformed, and numerous affairs were in their beginning; it was appropriate to wait for great peace and then slowly discuss editing and compilation.

units.zh: 欲且省禮局，並還尚書儀曹。
units.en: They proposed temporarily abolishing the ritual bureau and returning its functions to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.
units.literal: They wished temporarily to reduce the ritual bureau and return its functions altogether to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 詔旨云：「禮壞樂缺，故國異家殊，實宜以時修定，以爲永准。
units.en: The imperial edict read: "Ritual has fallen into ruin and music into neglect; that is why every state and every house follows different customs. The rites should indeed be revised and fixed in timely fashion, to serve as a permanent standard.
units.literal: The edict stated: "Ritual is ruined and music is lacking; therefore states differ and families vary. It is truly appropriate to revise and fix them in timely fashion, making them an eternal standard.

units.zh: 但頃之修撰，以情取人，不以學進；
units.en: But in recent compilations, men were chosen through personal favor rather than scholarly merit;
units.literal: But in recent editing and compilation, people were chosen by personal favor, not advanced by learning;

units.zh: 其掌知者，以貴總一，不以稽古，所以歷年不就，有名無實。
units.en: those placed in charge were selected for rank rather than knowledge of antiquity. That is why years passed without completion, and the project had a name but no substance.
units.literal: those in charge were unified by rank, not by investigation of antiquity. Therefore years passed without completion — there was a name but no substance.

units.zh: 此旣經國所先，外可議其人，人定，便卽撰次。」
units.en: Since this is a matter of first importance to the ordering of the state, the outer offices should nominate suitable men; once the personnel are settled, compilation should begin at once."
units.literal: Since this is what ordering the state puts first, the outer offices may discuss the personnel; once the men are fixed, then immediately compile and arrange."

units.zh: 於是尚書僕射沈約等參議，請五禮各置舊學士一人，人各自舉學士二人，相助抄撰。
units.en: Thereupon Shen Yue, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and others deliberated and proposed that each of the Five Rites should have one senior academician appointed, each of whom would in turn recommend two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.
units.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue and others deliberated and requested that for each of the Five Rites one senior academician be appointed, each man himself recommending two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.

units.zh: 其中有疑者，依前漢石渠、後漢白虎，隨源以聞，請旨斷決。
units.en: Where doubts arose, following the precedent of the Shiqu and Baihu conferences of Han, the matter would be reported with citations and submitted for imperial decision.
units.literal: Where there were doubts, following the precedents of Shiqu in Former Han and Baihu in Later Han, they were reported according to source for imperial decision.

units.zh: 乃以舊學士右軍記室參軍明山賓掌吉禮，中軍騎兵參軍嚴植之掌凶禮，中軍田曹行參軍兼太常丞賀蒨掌賓禮，征虜記室參軍陸璉掌軍禮，右軍參軍司馬裴掌嘉禮，尚書左丞何佟之總參其事。
units.en: Ming Shanbin, a former academician and Record-Office Aide on the Right Army staff, was placed in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Aide on the Central Army staff, of inauspicious rites; He Qian, acting Field Bureau Aide on the Central Army staff and concurrently Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, of guest rites; Lu Lian, Record-Office Aide to the General Who Conquers the Caitiffs, of military rites; Sima Pei, Staff Officer of the Right Army, of celebratory rites; and He Tongzhi, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, was given overall supervision of the project.
units.literal: Thereupon the senior academician Ming Shanbin, Recorder of the Right Army Staff, was put in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Commandant of the Central Army, was put in charge of inauspicious rites; He Qian, Acting Army Field Commandant of the Central Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was put in charge of guest rites; Lu Lian, Recorder of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was put in charge of military rites; Sima Pei, Army Staff Officer of the Right Army, was put in charge of celebratory rites; and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat He Tongzhi was given overall participation in the affair.

units.zh: 佟之亡後，以鎮北諮議參軍伏暅代之。
units.en: After He Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.
units.literal: After Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.

units.zh: 後又以暅代嚴植之掌凶禮。
units.en: Later Fu Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi as overseer of inauspicious rites.
units.literal: Later Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi in charge of inauspicious rites.

units.zh: 暅尋遷官，以《五經》博士繆昭掌凶禮。
units.en: Fu Xiong was soon transferred to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the "Five Classics," was placed in charge of inauspicious rites.
units.literal: Xiong soon transferred to another post, and Erudite of the Five Classics Miao Zhao was put in charge of inauspicious rites.

units.zh: 復以禮儀深廣，記載殘缺，宜須博論，共盡其致，更使鎮軍將軍丹陽尹沈約、太常卿張充及臣三人同參厥務。
units.en: Because ritual propriety was vast in scope and the surviving records were fragmentary, broad deliberation was needed to exhaust its full meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject — the three of us — were further appointed jointly to oversee the work.
units.literal: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and the records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed so that all might exhaust its meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject, three men, were further ordered jointly to participate in the task.

units.zh: 臣又奉別敕，總知其事。
units.en: Your subject also received a separate edict placing me in overall charge of the project.
units.literal: Your subject also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.

units.zh: 末又使中書侍郎周捨、庾於陵二人復豫參知。
units.en: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were also appointed to take part in deliberation.
units.literal: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were again ordered to participate in the deliberations.

units.zh: 若有疑義，所掌學士當職先立議，通諮五禮舊學士及參知，各言同異，條牒啓聞，決之制旨。
units.en: When a doubtful point arose, the academician responsible would first draft a proposal, consult the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the other participants, record each man's agreement or dissent, submit the matter in memorial, and await the emperor's decision.
units.literal: If there were doubtful points, the academician in charge of the duty would first establish a proposal, consult broadly with the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the participants in consultation, each stating agreement or difference; the items would be submitted in memorial for decision by imperial edict.

units.zh: 疑事旣多，歲時又積，制旨裁斷，其數不少。
units.en: The doubtful points were many, and the years accumulated; the number of imperial decisions handed down was considerable.
units.literal: Doubtful matters were already many, and years also accumulated; imperial edicts deciding them were not a few in number.

units.zh: 莫不網羅經誥，玉振金聲，義貫幽微，理入神契。
units.en: Every decision drew upon the canonical texts with the resonance of jade and gold; meaning reached into the subtlest depths, and principle attained a harmony that seemed almost divine.
units.literal: None failed to gather the canonical teachings, jade vibrating and gold sounding; meaning penetrated the subtle, and principle entered divine accord.

units.zh: 前儒所不釋，後學所未聞。
units.en: Points that earlier scholars had left unresolved were settled here; matters that later students had never heard explained were made clear.
units.literal: What former Confucians did not explain, later students had not heard.

units.zh: 凡諸奏決，皆載篇首，具列聖旨，爲不刊之則。
units.en: Every decision submitted and approved was recorded at the head of the relevant section, with the imperial intent fully set forth, to serve as an immutable standard.
units.literal: All memorial decisions were recorded at the head of each section, fully listing the sage intent, forming an unalterable standard.

units.zh: 洪規盛範，冠絕百王；
units.en: These grand regulations and magnificent models surpass those of all the kings of old;
units.literal: Grand regulations and flourishing models surpass all hundred kings;

units.zh: 茂實英聲，方垂千載。
units.en: their substance is rich and their renown splendid, and they will be handed down for a thousand years.
units.literal: abundant substance and outstanding renown will be handed down for a thousand years.

units.zh: 寧孝宣之能擬，豈孝章之足云。
units.en: Even Emperor Xuan of Han could scarcely be compared with this achievement — to say nothing of Emperor Zhang.
units.literal: Can even Emperor Xiaoxuan be compared? How could Emperor Xiaozhang suffice to mention?

units.zh: 五禮之職，事有繁簡，及其列畢，不得同時。
units.en: The work of the Five Rites varied in complexity, and the sections were completed at different times rather than all at once.
units.literal: The duties of the Five Rites had affairs both complex and simple; when each was arranged and completed, they could not all be finished at the same time.

units.zh: 《嘉禮儀注》以天監六年五月七日上尚書，合十有二秩，一百一十六卷，五百三十六條；
units.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, comprising twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;
units.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;

units.zh: 《賓禮儀注》以天監六年五月二十日上尚書，合十有七秩，一百三十三卷，五百四十五條；
units.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the same year, comprising seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;
units.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;

units.zh: 《軍禮儀注》以天監九年十月二十九日上尚書，合十有八秩，一百八十九卷，二百四十條；
units.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, comprising eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;
units.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, totaling eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;

units.zh: 《吉禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十日上尚書，合二十有六秩，二百二十四卷，一千五條；
units.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, comprising twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;
units.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;

units.zh: 《凶禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十七日上尚書，合四十有七秩，五百一十四卷，五千六百九十三條：大凡一百二十秩，一千一百七十六卷，八千一十九條。
units.en: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the same year, comprising forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles — in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.
units.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles: in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.

units.zh: 又列副秘閣及《五經》典書各一通，繕寫校定，以普通五年二月始獲洗畢。
units.en: Duplicate sets were also prepared for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one copy each. Copying and collation were completed, and fair copies were finally finished in the second month of the fifth year of Putong.
units.literal: Copies were also arranged for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one set each; copying, writing, and collation were completed, and in the second month of the fifth year of Putong they were finally finished in clean form.

units.zh: 竊以撰正履禮，歷代罕就，皇明在運，厥功克成。
units.en: I venture to observe that compiling and establishing ritual has rarely been brought to completion in any age; yet under Your Majesty's enlightened reign this great work has at last been achieved.
units.literal: I venture to consider that compiling, correcting, and practicing ritual has rarely been accomplished in successive generations; now under imperial brightness the age is in motion, and this merit has been able to succeed.

units.zh: 周代三千，舉其盈數；
units.en: In the Zhou, the rites were said to number three thousand, a round total;
units.literal: The Zhou era had three thousand, taking its full number;

units.zh: 今之八千，隨事附益。
units.en: today's eight thousand articles reflect additions made as circumstances required.
units.literal: today's eight thousand follow affairs in addition and increase.

units.zh: 質文相變，故其數兼倍，猶如八卦之爻，因而重之，錯綜成六十四也。
units.en: As substance and form change with the times, the number has naturally doubled — just as the lines of the eight trigrams, when doubled and interwoven, become sixty-four.
units.literal: Substance and form change each other; therefore the number is doubled — just like the lines of the eight trigrams, which are then doubled and interwoven to form sixty-four.

units.zh: 昔文武二王，所以綱紀周室，君臨天下，公旦修之，以致太平龍鳳之瑞。
units.en: In antiquity Kings Wen and Wu used ritual to order the Zhou house and rule the realm; the Duke of Zhou refined it, bringing about the age of peace marked by the auspicious appearances of dragon and phoenix.
units.literal: Formerly the two kings Wen and Wu thereby regulated the Zhou house, ruled over all under Heaven; the Duke of Zhou refined it, thereby attaining the auspicious signs of peace with dragon and phoenix.

units.zh: 自斯厥後，甫備茲日。
units.en: From that age until now, only on this day has such a work been fully completed.
units.literal: From that time until now, only on this day has it been fully prepared.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「其有繼周，雖百世可知。」
units.en: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations its way may be foreknown."
units.literal: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations it can be known."

units.zh: 豈所謂齊功比美者歟！
units.en: Is this not what is meant by matching Zhou in achievement and in splendor!
units.literal: Is this not what is called equal in achievement and comparable in beauty!

units.zh: 臣以庸識，謬司其任，淹留歷稔，允當斯責；
units.en: Your subject, with my mediocre understanding, was undeservedly entrusted with this charge; I have lingered in the post for many years and have truly borne its weight.
units.literal: Your subject, with mediocre understanding, was wrongly entrusted with this duty; lingering through accumulated years, I have truly borne this responsibility.

units.zh: 兼勒成之初，未遑表上，實由才輕務廣，思力不周，永言慚惕，無忘寤寐。
units.en: When the work was first completed, I had not yet submitted this memorial, truly because my ability was slight and the task vast, and my thought and strength were not equal to it. I remain ashamed and apprehensive, and the matter has never left my mind, waking or sleeping.
units.literal: Moreover, at the beginning when completion was achieved, I had no leisure to submit a memorial — truly because talent was slight and tasks were broad, thought and strength were not comprehensive. I always speak with shame and caution, never forgetting waking or sleeping.

units.zh: 自今春輿駕將親六師，搜尋軍禮，閱其條章，靡不該備。
units.en: Since this spring, as Your Majesty has prepared to lead the Six Armies in person, I have searched the military rites and reviewed their articles and regulations; all are comprehensive and complete.
units.literal: Since this spring the imperial carriage will personally lead the Six Armies; searching through military rites and examining their articles and regulations, none are not comprehensive and complete.

units.zh: 所謂郁郁文哉，煥乎洋溢，信可以懸諸日月，頒之天下者矣。
units.en: Truly it is richly cultured and brilliantly complete — a work that may be displayed beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout the realm.
units.literal: What is called richly cultured indeed, brilliantly overflowing — truly it can be suspended beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout all under Heaven.

units.zh: 愚心喜抃，彌思陳述；
units.en: My humble heart rejoices at this achievement, and I am all the more moved to report it;
units.literal: My foolish heart rejoices and claps hands; I all the more wish to set forth and state;

units.zh: 兼前後聯官，一時皆逝，臣雖倖存，耄已將及，慮皇世大典，遂闕騰奏，不任下情，輒具載撰修始末，并職掌人、所成卷秩、條目之數，謹拜表以聞。
units.en: Moreover, the officials who served before and after me have all passed away; though I alone survive, old age is already upon me. Fearing that this great canon of the imperial age might never be formally reported, and unable to suppress my earnest feeling, I have set forth in full the history of the compilation, the officials in charge, and the number of scrolls and articles completed, and respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty's notice.
units.literal: Moreover, the officials connected before and after all passed away at one time; though your subject survives by fortune, old age is already approaching. Fearing that the great canon of the imperial age would thus lack a submitted memorial, unable to bear my lower feelings, I have fully recorded the beginning and end of compilation and revision, together with the persons in charge, the scroll sections completed, and the number of articles, and respectfully bow with this memorial to report.

units.zh: 詔曰：「經禮大備，政典載弘，今詔有司，案以行事也。」
units.en: An edict read: "The canonical rites are now fully complete, and the governmental canon greatly enriched. Let the responsible offices implement them in practice."
units.literal: An edict stated: "The canonical rites are greatly complete, and the governmental canon is broadly enlarged. Now we order the responsible offices to follow them in conducting affairs."

units.zh: 又詔曰：「勉表如此。
units.en: Another edict read: "Mian's memorial is as stated.
units.literal: Another edict stated: "Mian's memorial is as this.

units.zh: 因革允𨤸，憲章孔備，功成業定，於是乎在。
units.en: Reform and preservation duly balanced, statutes and patterns fully complete; the work accomplished and the enterprise settled — all is fulfilled here.
units.literal: Changing and keeping what is suitable, statutes and patterns fully complete; achievement accomplished and enterprise settled — herein it lies.

units.zh: 可以光被八表，施諸百代，俾萬世之下，知斯文在斯。
units.en: It may shine across the eight directions and be handed down through a hundred generations, so that for ten thousand years to come men may know that this civilization endures here.
units.literal: It can radiate to the eight directions, be applied through a hundred generations, so that beneath ten thousand generations men may know that this culture is here.

units.zh: 主者其按以遵行，勿有失墜。」
units.en: Let the responsible officials review it and carry it out; let nothing be allowed to fall away."
units.literal: Let those in charge examine it and follow it; let nothing be lost or neglected."

units.zh: 尋加中書令，給親信二十人。
units.en: Soon afterward he was further appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.

units.zh: 勉以疾自陳，求解內任。
units.en: Mian pleaded illness in a memorial, asking to be relieved of his duties within the palace.
units.literal: Mian, citing illness, submitted a memorial requesting release from inner-court duties.

units.zh: 詔不許，乃令停下省，三日一朝，有事遣主書論決。
units.en: The edict refused; instead he was told to stay at the Secretariat without daily attendance, appearing at court every three days while routine business was referred to chief clerks for deliberation and decision.
units.literal: An edict did not permit it; instead he was ordered to remain at the Secretariat but cease daily attendance, coming to court every three days, with matters sent to chief clerks for discussion and decision.

units.zh: 腳疾轉劇，久闕朝覲，固陳求解，詔乃賚假，須疾差還省。
units.en: His foot ailment worsened, and after long absence from court he again pressed to resign; the emperor then granted him leave, with orders to return to office once he recovered.
units.literal: His foot ailment grew worse; having long missed court audience, he repeatedly requested release; an edict then granted him leave, requiring return to the Secretariat once the illness improved.

units.zh: 勉雖居顯位，不營產業，家無蓄積，俸祿分贍親族之窮乏者。
units.en: Though Mian held high office, he did not build up an estate; his household kept no reserves, and he divided his salary to support impoverished kinsmen.
units.literal: Though Mian held a prominent position, he did not pursue property; his household had no savings, and his salary was divided to support needy relatives.

units.zh: 門人故舊或從容致言。
units.en: Students and old friends would sometimes raise the matter with him in easy conversation.
units.literal: Students and old friends sometimes spoke to him at leisure.

units.zh: 勉乃答曰：「人遺子孫以財，我遺之以清白。
units.en: Mian answered: "People leave their children wealth; I leave them a name for integrity.
units.literal: Mian replied: "Others leave their descendants wealth; I leave them integrity.

units.zh: 子孫才也，則自致輜軿；
units.en: If a man's sons have ability, they will win fine carriages for themselves;
units.literal: If one's descendants have talent, they will obtain covered carriages on their own;

units.zh: 如其不才，終爲他有。」
units.en: if they lack talent, whatever wealth there is will end up in others' hands."
units.literal: if they lack talent, wealth will ultimately belong to others."

units.zh: 嘗爲書誡其子崧曰：
units.en: He once wrote a letter of admonition to his son Song, which read:
units.literal: He once wrote a letter admonishing his son Song, saying:

units.zh: 吾家世清廉，故常居貧素，至於產業之事，所未嘗言，非直不經營而已。
units.en: Our house has been honest for generations, and so we have always lived plainly. I have never so much as spoken of property — it is not simply that I have refused to manage it.
units.literal: Our family has been upright through the generations and thus has always lived in plain poverty. As for matters of property, I have never even spoken of them — not merely refrained from managing them.

units.zh: 薄躬遭逢，遂至今日，尊官厚祿，可謂備之。
units.en: My humble person, favored by circumstance, has risen to where I stand today; high rank and ample stipend — you might say I have them in full.
units.literal: My humble self, having met with fortune, has come to this day; high office and generous salary — one might say I possess them all.

units.zh: 每念叨竊若斯，豈由才致，仰藉先代風範及以福慶，故臻此耳。
units.en: Whenever I reflect on how unworthily I hold such eminence, I know it is not through my own merit; I owe it to the example of my forebears and to inherited good fortune — that alone has brought me here.
units.literal: Whenever I think how undeservedly I hold such rank, it is surely not through my own ability; I rely upon the moral bearing of earlier generations and upon accumulated blessings — that is how I have reached this.

units.zh: 古人所謂「以清白遺子孫，不亦厚乎！」
units.en: As the ancients said, "To bequeath integrity to one's descendants — is that not the richest gift?"
units.literal: What the ancients meant by "leaving integrity to one's descendants — is that not a generous legacy!"

units.zh: 又云：「遺子黃金滿籝，不如一經。」
units.en: And again: "To leave a son gold enough to fill a basket is inferior to leaving him one classic."
units.literal: It is also said: "To leave one's son a basket brimming with gold is not as good as leaving him one classic."

units.zh: 詳求此言，信非徒語。
units.en: Consider those words closely, and you will see they are no idle sayings.
units.literal: Reflecting carefully on these words, one finds they are truly not empty speech.

units.zh: 吾雖不敏，實有本志，庶得遵奉斯義，不敢墜失。
units.en: I am not clever, but this has always been my aim; I mean to live by that principle and not let it slip.
units.literal: Though I am not clever, I truly hold to this original resolve, hoping to follow this principle and not dare let it fall away.

units.zh: 所以顯貴以來，將三十載，門人故舊，亟薦便宜，或使創辟田園，或勸興立邸店，又欲舳艫運致，亦令貨殖聚斂。
units.en: In the nearly thirty years since I rose to prominence, students and old friends have again and again pressed practical schemes on me — some urging me to open fields and gardens, some to set up inns and shops, others to freight goods by river, all counseling trade and accumulation.
units.literal: Since I rose to eminence, nearly thirty years have passed; students and old friends have repeatedly urged expedient measures — some suggesting opening up estates and gardens, some urging the founding of inns and shops, others wishing to transport goods by boat, all recommending commercial profit and accumulation.

units.zh: 若此衆事，皆距而不納。
units.en: I have turned every such proposal away.
units.literal: Such proposals I have all rejected and refused.

units.zh: 非謂拔葵去織，且欲省息紛紜。
units.en: This is not the purism of pulling up melons and forbidding weaving at home; I simply want to spare myself the noise and bother.
units.literal: I do not mean this as pulling up melons and removing weaving; I simply wish to reduce and quiet the bustle.

units.zh: 中年聊於東田間營小園者，非在播藝，以要利入，正欲穿池種樹，少寄情賞。
units.en: In middle age I casually laid out a small garden on the eastern fields — not to farm for profit, but to dig a pond, plant trees, and find a little room for quiet delight.
units.literal: In middle age I briefly laid out a small garden among the eastern fields — not to cultivate crops for profit, but simply to dig a pond and plant trees, giving a little scope to refined pleasure.

units.zh: 又以郊際閑曠，終可爲宅，儻獲懸車致事，實欲歌哭於斯。
units.en: The suburbs are open and spacious and could serve as a home; if I should retire at seventy, I truly mean to spend my remaining days there in joy and sorrow alike.
units.literal: Also because the outskirts are open and spacious and could in the end serve as a dwelling — if I should obtain release from office at the age of seventy, I truly mean to sing and weep my days there.

units.zh: 慧日、十住等，旣應營婚，又須住止，吾清明門宅，無相容處。
units.en: Huiri, Shizhu, and the others must marry and need places to live, yet my house at Qingming Gate has no space for them.
units.literal: Huiri, Shizhu, and the others must both arrange marriages and need places to live; my residence at Qingming Gate has no room to accommodate them.

units.zh: 所以爾者，亦復有以；
units.en: There is reason for this as well;
units.literal: The reason for this, moreover, has its grounds;

units.zh: 前割西邊施宣武寺，旣失西廂，不復方幅，意亦謂此逆旅舍耳，何事須華？
units.en: I earlier gave the western wing to Xuanwu Temple; without it the house is no longer a proper square. I think of it as a roadside inn — why should it be grand?
units.literal: Previously I ceded the western portion to Xuanwu Temple; having lost the west wing, the compound is no longer square and whole. I also regard it as nothing but an inn — why must it be splendid?

units.zh: 常恨時人謂是我宅。
units.en: I have always resented people calling it my mansion.
units.literal: I have always resented that people of the day call it my mansion.

units.zh: 古往今來，豪富繼踵，高門甲第，連闥洞房，宛其死矣，定是誰室？
