units.en: From ancient times to now, the rich have followed one after another — great gates and mansions, halls linked to chambers. When the owner dies, whose house is it?
units.literal: From antiquity to the present, the wealthy succeed one another; grand gates and mansions, linked halls and inner chambers — when the owner is dead, whose house are they?

units.zh: 但不能不爲培塿之山，聚石移果，雜以花卉，以娛休沐，用誌性靈。
units.en: Still, one cannot help raising a little hill, gathering stones, moving fruit trees, and planting flowers — to enjoy days of rest and give the spirit its due.
units.literal: Yet one cannot but raise a mound of earth here and there, gather stones and transplant fruit trees, mix in flowers, to delight in days of rest, and give expression to one's inner spirit.

units.zh: 隨便架立，不在廣大，惟功德處，小以爲好。
units.en: Build as convenience allows; size is not the point — only where good is to be done do I prefer things modest.
units.literal: Build whatever is convenient; vastness is not the aim — only where merit is to be done is smallness preferred.

units.zh: 所以內中逼促，無復房宇。
units.en: That is why the inner quarters are cramped and there is no spare room.
units.literal: That is why the interior is cramped and there is no surplus room.

units.zh: 近營東邊兒孫二宅，乃藉十住南還之資，其中所須，猶爲不少，旣牽挽不至，又不可中塗而輟，郊間之園，遂不辦保，貨與韋黯，乃獲百金，成就兩宅，已消其半。
units.en: Recently I built two houses to the east for my children and grandchildren, using the money Shizhu brought back from the south; even so, much was still needed. When further funds failed to arrive and the work could not be abandoned halfway, I could not keep the suburban garden and sold it to Wei An for a hundred gold pieces — enough to finish both houses, though half was already gone.
units.literal: Recently I built two residences eastward for children and grandchildren, drawing on the funds Shizhu brought back from the south; what was still required was considerable. Since funds could not be raised in time, and the work could not be halted midway, I was unable to keep the suburban garden and sold it to Wei An, obtaining a hundred gold pieces; the two houses were completed, consuming half of it.

units.zh: 尋園價所得，何以至此？
units.en: You may ask how the garden fetched so high a price.
units.literal: You may wonder how the sale of the garden fetched so much.

units.zh: 由吾經始歷年，粗已成立，桃李茂密，桐竹成陰，塍陌交通，渠畎相屬，華樓迥榭，頗有臨眺之美；
units.en: Because I had worked on it for years and it was largely finished: peaches and plums in thick leaf, paulownia and bamboo in shade, field paths crossing, irrigation channels linked, elegant towers and distant pavilions with fine views;
units.literal: Because I had founded it over many years and it was roughly complete: peach and plum trees dense, paulownia and bamboo casting shade, paths crossing fields, irrigation ditches linked together, elegant towers and distant pavilions with fine views for gazing afar;

units.zh: 孤峰叢薄，不無糾紛之興。
units.en: solitary peaks and brushy slopes — enough to stir the mind to verse.
units.literal: solitary peaks and thickets — not without stirrings of poetic feeling.

units.zh: 瀆中並饒菰蔣，湖裏殊富芰蓮。
units.en: The ditch teemed with wild rice and rushes; the lake was rich in water chestnuts and lotus.
units.literal: The channel abounds in wild rice and rushes; the lake is rich in water chestnuts and lotus.

units.zh: 雖云人外，城闕密邇，韋生欲之，亦雅有情趣。
units.en: Though it lay outside the city, the walls were near; Wei wanted it, and no wonder — it had real charm.
units.literal: Though it is said to be beyond the city of men, the walls are close by; Wei wanted it, and with good reason — it had refined charm.

units.zh: 追述此事，非有吝心，蓋是筆勢所至耳。
units.en: I tell this story not from regret or stinginess, but because my pen ran on.
units.literal: In recounting this, I feel no regret or stinginess; it is simply where the pen carried me.

units.zh: 憶謝靈運《山家詩》云：「中爲天地物，今成鄙夫有。」
units.en: I remember Xie Lingyun's "Mountain Dwelling Poem": "What was once Heaven and Earth's now belongs to a common man."
units.literal: I recall Xie Lingyun's "Mountain Dwelling Poem": "What was once a thing of Heaven and Earth now belongs to a common man."

units.zh: 吾此園有之二十載矣，今爲天地物，物之與我，相校幾何哉！
units.en: I held this garden twenty years; now it is Heaven and Earth's again — between the place and me, how great is the difference!
units.literal: I have possessed this garden for twenty years; now it returns to being a thing of Heaven and Earth — between the thing and me, how great is the difference!

units.zh: 此吾所餘，今以分汝，營小田舍，親累旣多，理亦須此。
units.en: This is what I have left; I now give you your share to set up a small farm — with so many mouths in the family, you need it.
units.literal: This is what remains to me; I now divide it with you to establish a small farmstead — with so many dependents in the family, it is only reasonable to need this.

units.zh: 且釋氏之教，以財物謂之外命；
units.en: Besides, Buddhist teaching calls wealth and goods the outer life;
units.literal: Moreover, in Buddhist teaching wealth and goods are called the outer life;

units.zh: 儒典亦稱「何以聚人曰財」。
units.en: and the Confucian canon says, "By what do men gather? By wealth."
units.literal: the Confucian classics also say, "By what do men gather together? By wealth."

units.zh: 況汝曹常情，安得忘此。
units.en: And you are only human — how could you ignore that?
units.literal: How much more so for you — ordinary human feelings — how could you forget this?

units.zh: 聞汝所買姑孰田地，甚爲舄鹵，彌復何安。
units.en: I hear the land you bought at Gushu is poor and salty — how can that comfort me?
units.literal: I hear the land you bought at Gushu is very salinous and poor — how could that set my mind at ease?

units.zh: 所以如此，非物競故也。
units.en: I say this not from rivalry over possessions.
units.literal: My concern is not from competing over property.

units.zh: 雖事異寢丘，聊可髣髴。
units.en: Though this differs from the case of Qinqiu (Sleeping Mound), it may serve as a rough likeness.
units.literal: Though the matter differs from Qinqiu, it may serve as a rough likeness.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「居家理治，可移於官。」
units.en: Confucius said, "Good household governance can be carried into public office."
units.literal: Confucius said: "Ordering one's household well may be transferred to office."

units.zh: 旣已營之，宜使成立。
units.en: Since you have begun, you should see it through.
units.literal: Since you have begun it, you should bring it to completion.

units.zh: 進退兩亡，更貽恥笑。
units.en: To advance and fail, or to retreat halfway — either way brings shame.
units.literal: Advancing and retreating both lost — that would only invite mockery.

units.zh: 若有所收穫，汝可自分贍內外大小，宜令得所，非吾所知，又復應沾之諸女耳。
units.en: If there is a harvest, divide it yourself among the household, great and small, as each deserves — the details are yours to manage; only remember the daughters who should share in it.
units.literal: If there is any harvest, you may yourself distribute support to those within and without, great and small, seeing that each has what's fitting — as for details, that is not for me to know; only that the daughters entitled to a share should receive one.

units.zh: 汝旣居長，故有此及。
units.en: Because you are the eldest, I write to you about this.
units.literal: Since you are the eldest, I address you on this.

units.zh: 凡爲人長，殊復不易，當使中外諧緝，人無間言，先物後己，然後可貴。
units.en: To be the eldest is no easy thing: keep kin and household in harmony, leave no room for gossip, put others before yourself — only then are you worth respect.
units.literal: To be the eldest in a family is truly not easy; one must keep inner and outer circles in harmony, so that no one has complaint, putting others before oneself — only then is one worthy of respect.

units.zh: 老生云：「後其身而身先。」
units.en: The Old Master said, "Put yourself last and you will be first."
units.literal: Laozi said: "Put yourself behind and you will be ahead."

units.zh: 若能爾者，更招巨利。
units.en: Live that way and you will gain much.
units.literal: If you can do this, you will reap great benefit.

units.zh: 汝當自勗，見賢思齊，不宜忽略以棄日也。
units.en: Exhort yourself: when you see the worthy, strive to match them; do not waste your days in idleness.
units.literal: You must urge yourself on, seeing the worthy and thinking to equal them; you must not neglect and waste your days.

units.zh: 非徒棄日，乃是棄身，身名美惡，豈不大哉！
units.en: That is not merely wasting days — it is wasting your life; the honor or disgrace of your name — is that not weighty!
units.literal: Not merely wasting days — you waste yourself; the beauty or ugliness of one's person and name — is that not momentous!

units.zh: 可不慎歟？
units.en: Can you not be on your guard?
units.literal: Can one not be careful?

units.zh: 今之所敕，略言此意。
units.en: What I urge upon you now is only this in brief.
units.literal: What I admonish today briefly states this intention.

units.zh: 正謂爲家已來，不事資產，旣立墅舍，以乖舊業，陳其始末，無愧懷抱。
units.en: I mean that though I have never pursued property for the household, I have now built a villa and departed from my old way — yet in telling the whole story, my conscience is clear.
units.literal: I mean precisely that since taking charge of the household I have not pursued assets; having now established a villa, I depart from my old practice — yet in recounting the whole course, I have nothing to reproach in my conscience.

units.zh: 兼吾年時朽暮，心力稍殫，牽課奉公，略不克舉，其中餘暇，裁可自休。
units.en: I am old now, my strength nearly gone; bound to public duty, I can barely keep up, and what little time remains is barely enough for rest.
units.literal: Moreover I am now old and declining; my strength is largely spent. Dragged by duties to serve the state, I can barely manage; whatever leisure remains barely suffices for my own rest.

units.zh: 或復冬日之陽，夏日之陰，良辰美景，文案間隙，負杖躡屩，逍遙陋館，臨池觀魚，披林聽鳥，濁酒一杯，彈琴一曲，求數刻之暫樂，庶居常以待終，不宜復勞家間細務。
units.en: On a winter sun or summer shade, on fine days amid lovely scenes, in brief gaps between documents — staff in hand, sandals on my feet, wandering my humble lodge, watching fish in the pond, listening to birds in the grove, a cup of plain wine, a tune on the zither, a few moments' joy before the end — I should not be troubled again with household trifles.
units.literal: On winter sun or summer shade, fine days and lovely scenes, in intervals between documents — leaning on my staff, slipping on straw sandals, roaming my humble lodge, gazing at fish by the pond, listening to birds in the groves, a cup of coarse wine, a stretch upon the zither, seeking a few moments' pleasure, hoping to abide peacefully until the end — I ought not again be burdened with household minutiae.

units.zh: 汝交關旣定，此書又行，凡所資須，付給如別。
units.en: Your affairs are settled, and with this letter everything required will be provided as listed separately.
units.literal: Your arrangements are settled, this letter goes forth; whatever is needed shall be supplied as separately indicated.

units.zh: 自茲以後，吾不復言及田事，汝亦勿復與吾言之。
units.en: From now on I will not speak of the farm, and you must not speak of it to me either.
units.literal: From now on I shall speak of field affairs no more; you also must not speak of them to me again.

units.zh: 假使堯水湯旱，吾豈知如何；
units.en: Even if Yao's flood or Tang's drought should come, what would I know?
units.literal: Even if floods like Yao's or drought like Tang's should come, what would I know of it?

units.zh: 若其滿庾盈箱，爾之幸遇。
units.en: If the bins are full and the granaries overflow, that is your good luck.
units.literal: If bins overflow and granaries brim, that is your good fortune.

units.zh: 如斯之事，並無俟令吾知也。
units.en: Matters like that need not be reported to me.
units.literal: Such matters need not await my being told.

units.zh: 《記》云：「夫孝者，善繼人之志，善述人之事。」
units.en: The "Record" says, "Filial piety is to continue another's aim well and carry on another's work well."
units.literal: The "Record" says: "Filial piety means well continuing another's will and well carrying out another's affairs."

units.zh: 今且望汝全吾此志，則無所恨矣。
units.en: For now I ask only that you honor this wish of mine, and I shall have no regret.
units.literal: For now I hope you will fulfill this will of mine, and then I shall have no regret.

units.zh: 勉第二子悱卒，痛悼甚至，不欲久廢王務，乃爲《答客喻》。
units.en: When Mian's second son Fei died, his grief was profound; unwilling to neglect state business for long, he wrote "Answer to the Guest's Remonstrance."
units.literal: When Mian's second son Fei died, his grief was extreme; unwilling to long neglect state affairs, he composed "Answer to the Guest's Remonstrance."

units.zh: 其辭曰：
units.en: It reads:
units.literal: Its words read:

units.zh: 普通五年春二月丁丑，余第二息晉安內史悱喪之問至焉，舉家傷悼，心情若隕。
units.en: In the second month of spring, fifth year of Putong, on day dingchou, word arrived that my second son Fei, Interior Secretary of Jin'an, had died; the whole household grieved, our hearts as though they had dropped from the sky.
units.literal: In the second month of spring in the fifth year of Putong, on day dingchou, word came of the death of my second son Fei, Interior Secretary of Jin'an; the whole household mourned, hearts as if fallen.

units.zh: 二宮並降中使，以相慰勗，親游賓客，畢來弔問，輒慟哭失聲，悲不自已，所謂父子天性，不知涕之所從來也。
units.en: Both palaces sent envoys to comfort and encourage us; kin, friends, and guests all came to mourn. I would break into uncontrollable wailing, grief I could not restrain — the bond between father and son; I did not know where the tears came from.
units.literal: Both palaces sent palace envoys to console and encourage; relatives, friends, and guests all came to offer condolences. I would burst into wailing beyond control, grief unchecked — what is called the nature of father and son; I knew not whence the tears came.

units.zh: 於是門人慮其肆情所鐘，容致委頓，乃斂衽而進曰：「僕聞古往今來，理運之常數；
units.en: Then his students, fearing that such unchecked grief might exhaust him, straightened their robes and came forward: "We have heard that from ancient times to the present, principle and fate follow fixed laws;
units.literal: Then my students, fearing his abandoned emotion might waste his strength, straightened their robes and stepped forward, saying: "Your servant has heard that from antiquity to the present, the order of principle and fate follows constant patterns;

units.zh: 春榮秋落，氣象之定期。
units.en: spring's flourishing and autumn's decline are the appointed seasons of nature.
units.literal: spring glory and autumn fall are fixed seasons of the natural order.

units.zh: 人居其間，譬諸逆旅，生寄死歸，著於通論，是以深識之士，悠爾忘懷。
units.en: Men live between them like travelers at an inn: life is a sojourn, death a return home — so the common teaching runs; therefore the wise man lightly lets go.
units.literal: Men dwell between them like guests at an inn; life is lodging, death is return — so runs the common teaching; hence the deeply knowing gentleman lightly forgets and releases.

units.zh: 東門歸無之旨，見稱往哲；
units.en: The lesson of 'no grief at the eastern gate' was praised by the sages of old;
units.literal: The meaning of 'return without sorrow at the eastern gate' has been praised by sages of old;

units.zh: 西河喪明之過，取誚友朋。
units.en: while blinding oneself in grief at Xihe brought reproach from friends.
units.literal: the fault of mourning blindness at Xihe drew mockery from friends.

units.zh: 足下受遇於朝，任居端右，憂深責重，休戚是均，宜其遺情下流，止哀加飯，上存奉國，俯示隆家。
units.en: You are favored by the court, hold the highest office on the right, and bear heavy cares; joy and sorrow touch you alike. You should set grief aside, stop mourning and take food — serve the state above, and show your household strength below.
units.literal: You have been favored by the court, hold the foremost post on the right, bear heavy cares and grave responsibility, sharing weal and woe alike. You ought to set aside lower emotion, stop grief and take food; above, preserve service to the state; below, display the flourishing of your house.

units.zh: 豈可縱此無益，同之兒女，傷神損識，或虧生務。
units.en: How can you indulge useless grief like a child, injuring your spirit and dulling your mind, perhaps failing in the work of life?
units.literal: How can you indulge this useless grief like women and children, harming spirit and diminishing wisdom, perhaps failing in the duties of life?

units.zh: 門下竊議，咸爲君侯不取也。」
units.en: We of your household have discussed this privately, and all agree it ill becomes you, my lord."
units.literal: We of your household privately discuss and all deem this unworthy of you, Lord."

units.zh: 余雪泣而答曰：「彭殤之達義，延吳之雅言，亦常聞之矣；
units.en: I wiped away my tears and replied: "I too have often heard the wisdom of viewing long life and early death alike, and the noble words of Yanling Jizi and Dongmen Wu;
units.literal: I answered, wiping away my tears: "I too have often heard the enlightened teaching concerning Pengzu and the short-lived, and the refined words of Yanling Jizi and Dongmen Wu;

units.zh: 顧所以未能弭意者，請陳其說。
units.en: yet why I cannot calm my heart — let me explain.
units.literal: yet why I cannot quiet my mind — allow me to set forth my reason.

units.zh: 夫植樹階庭，欽柯葉之茂；
units.en: Plant a tree in the courtyard and you delight in its leafy branches;
units.literal: When one plants a tree in the courtyard, one delights in the fullness of branch and leaf;

units.zh: 爲山累仞，惜覆簣之功。
units.en: raise a mountain many ren high and you regret even one basket spilled.
units.literal: building a mountain to many ren, one cherishes even the work of a basket overturned.

units.zh: 故秀而不實，尼父爲之歎息；
units.en: That is why Confucius sighed over 'flowering without fruit';
units.literal: Thus 'flowering yet bearing no fruit' — the Master sighed for it;

units.zh: 析彼歧路，楊子所以留連。
units.en: and why Yangzi lingered at the parting of the roads.
units.literal: parting at the forked road — Yangzi lingered therefore.

units.zh: 事有可深，聖賢靡抑。
units.en: When feeling runs deep, even sages do not forbid it.
units.literal: When a matter admits of deep feeling, even sages do not restrain it.

units.zh: 今吾所悲，亦以悱始逾立歲，孝悌之至，自幼而長，文章之美，得之天然，好學不倦，居無塵雜，多所著述，盈帙滿笥，淡然得失之際，不見喜慍之容。
units.en: What I mourn is that Fei had just passed thirty: filial and fraternal from childhood, gifted in letters by nature, tireless in study, living without worldly clutter, writing until scrolls and cases overflowed, calm in gain and loss, never showing joy or anger on his face.
units.literal: What I mourn is this: Fei had just passed thirty; filial piety and brotherly respect reached their height, growing from childhood; literary grace came by nature; he loved learning without weariness; his dwelling was free of worldly dust; he wrote extensively, scrolls and cases overflowing; in the face of gain and loss he was tranquil, showing neither joy nor anger.

units.zh: 及翰飛東朝，參伍盛列，其所遊往，皆一時才俊，賦詩頌詠，終日忘疲。
units.en: When he rose in the Eastern Court and stood among the foremost, those he kept company with were the finest men of the day; composing and reciting poetry, he forgot weariness from morning to night.
units.literal: When he took wing in the Eastern Court, ranking among the foremost, those he consorted with were all talents of the age; composing and chanting poetry, he forgot fatigue all day long.

units.zh: 每從容謂吾以遭逢時來，位隆任要，當應推賢下士，先物後身，然後可以報恩明主，克保元吉。
units.en: He would calmly tell me that having risen in fortunate times to high rank and heavy responsibility, one must promote the worthy, defer to men of talent, and put others first — only then could one repay the enlightened sovereign and keep fortune secure.
units.literal: He would calmly tell me that having met with the times and risen to high rank and weighty duty, one should promote the worthy and defer to gentlemen, putting others before oneself — only then could one repay the enlightened lord and secure great fortune.

units.zh: 俾余二紀之中，忝竊若是，幸無大過者，繄此子之助焉。
units.en: That in twenty years I have held such rank unworthily yet avoided great fault — I owe to this son.
units.literal: That in two decades I have undeservedly held such rank yet fortunately committed no great fault — it was through this son's help.

units.zh: 自出閩區，政存清靜，冀其旋反，少慰衰暮，言念今日，眇然長往。
units.en: Since he left for Min, his rule was quiet and clean; I hoped for his return to comfort my old age — but today he is gone forever.
units.literal: Since he left for Min lands, his governance was marked by quiet purity; I hoped for his return to comfort my declining years — thinking of today, he has departed forever.

units.zh: 加以闔棺千里之外，未知歸骨之期，雖復無情之倫，庸詎不痛於昔！
units.en: And now the coffin is sealed a thousand li away, with no knowing when his bones will return — even the hardest heart could not but grieve as men have always grieved!
units.literal: Added to this, the coffin is closed a thousand li away; the day of returning his bones is unknown — though one were utterly without feeling, how could one not grieve as in times past!

units.zh: 夷甫孩抱中物，尚盡慟以待賓；
units.en: Wang Yan, for a child still in swaddling clothes, mourned fully before receiving guests;
units.literal: Xiangfu, for a child still in arms, yet fully mourned to receive guests;

units.zh: 安仁未及七旬，猶殷勤於詞賦。
units.en: Pan An, before seventy days had passed, still poured his grief into verse.
units.literal: Anren, before seventy days had passed, still poured feeling into rhapsodies.

units.zh: 況夫名立宦成，半途而廢者，亦焉可已已哉。
units.en: How much more when name and office were established and then cut short midway — how can grief be stilled!
units.literal: How much more when fame is established and office achieved, yet cut off midway — how can grief be restrained!

units.zh: 求其此懷，可謂苗實之義。
units.en: Measured by that feeling, this may be called the grief of the bud that never bore fruit.
units.literal: Seeking this feeling, one may call it the meaning of the budding and the fruit.

units.zh: 諸賢旣貽格言，喻以大理，卽日輟哀，命駕修職事焉。」
units.en: When my friends had offered their wise counsel and explained the larger principle, I ceased mourning that very day, took up my carriage, and returned to my official duties."
units.literal: The worthies having bestowed maxims and instructed me in the great principle, that very day I ceased mourning, ordered my carriage, and returned to my official duties."

units.zh: 中大通三年，又以疾自陳，移授特進、右光祿大夫、侍中、中衛將軍，置佐史，餘如故。
units.en: In Zhongdatong 3, Mian again submitted a statement because of illness, and was transferred to Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with staff officers established for him; the rest remained as before.
units.literal: In Zhongdatong 3, Mian again submitted a statement because of illness, and was transferred to Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with staff officers established for him; the rest remained as before.

units.zh: 增親信四十人。
units.en: His trusted attendants were increased by forty.
units.literal: His trusted attendants were increased by forty.

units.zh: 兩宮參問，冠蓋結轍；
units.en: The two palaces sent inquiries, and the tracks of capped carriages joined one another;
units.literal: The two palaces sent inquiries, and the tracks of capped carriages joined one another;

units.zh: 服膳醫藥，皆資天府。
units.en: his clothing, meals, medicine, and drugs were all supplied from the imperial treasury.
units.literal: his clothing, meals, medicine, and drugs were all supplied from the imperial treasury.

units.zh: 有敕每欲臨幸，勉以拜伏有虧，頻啓停出，詔許之，遂停輿駕。
units.en: Whenever there was an edict intending to visit him, Mian, because he could not properly bow and prostrate himself, repeatedly petitioned that the outing be stopped. The edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage was therefore halted.
units.literal: Whenever there was an edict intending to visit him, Mian, because he could not properly bow and prostrate himself, repeatedly petitioned that the outing be stopped. The edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage was therefore halted.

units.zh: 大同元年，卒，時年七十。
units.en: In Datong 1, he died, aged seventy.
units.literal: In Datong 1, he died, aged seventy.

units.zh: 高祖聞而流涕，卽日車駕臨殯，乃詔贈特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，餘並如故。
units.en: When Gaozu heard, he shed tears, and that same day the imperial carriage visited the bier. An edict then posthumously granted Mian the offices of Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the rest all as before.
units.literal: When Gaozu heard, he shed tears, and that same day the imperial carriage visited the bier. An edict then posthumously granted Mian the offices of Specially Advanced, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the rest all as before.

units.zh: 給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。
units.en: He was supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothes.
units.literal: He was supplied an imperial coffin from Dongyuan, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothes.

units.zh: 贈錢二十萬，布百匹。
units.en: He was granted two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.
units.literal: He was granted two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.

units.zh: 皇太子亦舉哀朝堂。
units.en: The crown prince also held mourning for him in the court hall.
units.literal: The crown prince also held mourning for him in the court hall.

units.zh: 諡曰簡肅公。
units.en: His posthumous title was Duke Jiansu.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jiansu.

units.zh: 勉善屬文，勤著述，雖當機務，下筆不休。
units.en: Mian was a skilled writer and a prolific author; even while burdened with the most urgent state business, he never stopped writing.
units.literal: Mian was skilled at composing texts and diligent in writing; though occupied with crucial affairs, his brush never stopped.

units.zh: 嘗以起居注煩雜，乃加刪撰爲《流別起居注》六百卷；
units.en: Finding the Daily Records unwieldy, he revised and abridged them into six hundred scrolls entitled "Classified Daily Records";
units.literal: Once, because the Daily Records were cumbersome and disorderly, he revised and compiled them into six hundred scrolls of "Classified Daily Records";

units.zh: 《左丞彈事》五卷；
units.en: "Memorials of Impeachment by the Left Assistant Director," in five scrolls;
units.literal: "Memorials of Impeachment by the Left Assistant Director," five scrolls;

units.zh: 在選曹，撰《選品》五卷；
units.en: while at the Selection Bureau, he compiled "Ranks of Selection" in five scrolls;
units.literal: while in the Selection Bureau, he compiled "Ranks of Selection," five scrolls;

units.zh: 齊時，撰《太廟祝文》二卷；
units.en: under Qi he compiled "Prayer Texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple" in two scrolls;
units.literal: during Qi, he compiled "Prayer Texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple," two scrolls;

units.zh: 以孔釋二教殊途同歸，撰《會林》五十卷。
units.en: Believing that Confucian and Buddhist teaching, though their paths differ, reach the same end, he compiled "Forest of Convergences" in fifty scrolls.
units.literal: Because the Confucian and Buddhist teachings, though paths differ, return to the same end, he compiled "Forest of Convergences," fifty scrolls.

units.zh: 凡所著前後二集四十五卷，又爲《婦人集》十卷，皆行於世。
units.en: His collected works in two series totaled forty-five scrolls, and he also compiled "Anthology of Women" in ten scrolls; all were in circulation.
units.literal: In all, his earlier and later collected works totaled forty-five scrolls; he also compiled "Anthology of Women," ten scrolls — all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 大同三年，故佐史尚書左丞劉覽等詣闕陳勉行狀，請刊石紀德，卽降詔許立碑於墓云。
units.en: In the third year of Datong, Liu Lan, former staff officer and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and others presented a report on Mian's conduct at court and asked that a stone be carved to commemorate his virtue. An edict was promptly issued authorizing a stele at his tomb.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong, the former staff officer and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Liu Lan and others came to the palace to present Mian's conduct report and requested that stone be carved to record his virtue; an edict was immediately issued permitting a stele to be erected at his tomb.

units.zh: 悱字敬業，幼聰敏，能屬文。
units.en: Xu Fei, whose courtesy name was Jingye, was clever as a boy and could already compose literary pieces.
units.literal: Fei, styled Jingye, in youth was clever and keen and could compose texts.

units.zh: 起家著作佐郎，轉太子舍人，掌書記之任。
units.en: He entered office as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and was later made Attendant of the Heir Apparent, in charge of records and correspondence.
units.literal: He began his career as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, holding charge of documents and records.

units.zh: 累遷洗馬、中舍人，猶管書記。
units.en: He rose through the ranks to Groom of the Heir Apparent and Central Attendant, while continuing to manage records and correspondence.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Groom and Central Attendant, still managing documents and records.

units.zh: 出入宮坊者歷稔，以足疾出爲湘東王友，遷晉安內史。
units.en: He had served in the Eastern Palace for many years. Because of a foot ailment he left court to become Companion to the King of Xiangdong and was later appointed Administrator of Jin'an.
units.literal: Entering and leaving the palace quarters for many years, because of foot ailment he went out to serve as Companion to the King of Xiangdong and was transferred to Administrator of Jin'an.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：徐勉少而厲志忘食，發憤脩身，慎言行，擇交遊；
units.en: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: "In youth Xu Mian disciplined his will until he forgot to eat, roused himself to cultivate his character, was careful in speech and conduct, and chose his companions with care;"
units.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: "Xu Mian in youth steeled his will and forgot food, roused his spirit to cultivate himself, was cautious in word and deed, and chose his companions carefully;"

units.zh: 加運屬興王，依光日月，故能明經術以綰青紫，出閭閻而取卿相。
units.en: when fortune favored the founding emperor and he basked in imperial favor, he was able to master the classics and win high office, rising from common streets to minister and chancellor.
units.literal: added to this, fortune belonged to the rising king and he rested in the light of sun and moon; thus he could clarify classical learning to bind on purple and blue, and leave the lanes and alleys to take the rank of minister and chancellor.

units.zh: 及居重任，竭誠事主，動師古始，依則先王，提衡端軌，物無異議，爲梁宗臣，盛矣。
units.en: Once he held great office, he served his sovereign with complete devotion, taking antiquity as his guide and the former kings as his model. He held the scales of justice even, and none disputed his judgments — a pillar minister of Liang indeed, and a splendid one.
units.literal: When he held heavy responsibility, he devoted his heart in serving his lord, taking antiquity as his teacher in every move and following the former kings as his rule; holding the balance and setting the standard straight, nothing met with dissent — as a pillar minister of Liang, how splendid!

units.en: [1] Endnote marker.
units.literal: [1] Endnote marker.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 王亮 張稷 王瑩
units.en: Wang Liang; Zhang Ji; Wang Ying
units.literal: Wang Liang; Zhang Ji; Wang Ying

units.zh: 王亮字奉叔，琅邪臨沂人，晉丞相導之六世孫也。
units.en: Wang Liang, styled Fengshu, came from Linyi in Langye—a sixth-generation descendant of Jin Chancellor Dao.
units.literal: Wang Liang, styled Fengshu, was a native of Linyi in Langye; he was sixth-generation descendant of Jin Chancellor Dao.

units.zh: 尚書左丞范縝起曰：「司徒謝朏本有虛名，陛下擢之如此，前尚書令王亮頗有治實，陛下棄之如彼，是愚臣所不知。」
units.en: Left assistant director Fan Zhen rose and said, "Grand Marshal Xie Fei had only empty fame, yet Your Majesty raised him so; former director Wang Liang had real governing merit, yet Your Majesty cast him off so—this dull minister cannot understand."
units.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen rose and said: "Grand Marshal Xie Fei originally had only empty fame, yet Your Majesty raised him thus; former Director Wang Liang truly had governing merit, yet Your Majesty cast him off like that—this a dull minister cannot understand."

units.zh: 風聞尚書左丞臣范縝，自晉安還，語人云：「我不詣餘人，惟詣王亮；
units.en: I have heard that left assistant director Fan Zhen, returning from Jin'an, said, "I visit no one but Wang Liang;
units.literal: I have heard that Left Assistant Director Fan Zhen, returning from Jin'an, told people: "I do not visit others, only Wang Liang;

units.zh: 不餉餘人，惟餉王亮。」
units.en: I give gifts to no one but Wang Liang."
units.literal: I do not give gifts to others, only Wang Liang."

units.zh: 縝不答所問，而橫議沸騰，遂貶裁司徒臣朏，褒舉庶人王亮。
units.en: Zhen did not answer what was asked but poured out reckless talk, disparaging grand marshal Tiao and praising the commoner Wang Liang.
units.literal: Zhen did not answer what was asked but launched a torrent of reckless talk, disparaging Grand Marshal Tiao and praising the commoner Wang Liang.

units.zh: 稷召尚書右僕射王亮等列坐殿前西鐘下，謂曰：「昔桀有昏德，鼎遷于殷；
units.en: Ji summoned Right Vice Director Wang Liang and others to sit before the western bell in the hall and said, "Of old Jie had dark virtue, and the tripod moved to Yin;
units.literal: Ji summoned Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang and others to sit in a row before the western bell in the hall and said: "Of old Jie had dark virtue, and the tripod moved to Yin;

units.zh: 王亮之居亂世，勢位見矣。
units.en: Wang Liang's standing in chaotic times—rank and position were plain to see.
units.literal: Wang Liang's standing in a chaotic age—his rank and position were plain to see.

units.zh: 諡曰煬子。
units.en: Posthumous title: Son Yang.
units.literal: Posthumous title: Son Yang.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，遷侍中、尚書令、中軍將軍，引參佐命，封豫寧縣公，邑二千戶。
units.en: When Gaozu took the mandate, Liang became attendant, director of the masters of writing, and central army general, drawn into founding the state, and was enfeoffed duke of Yuning with two thousand households.
units.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted to Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Central Army General, drawn into assisting the mandate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuning with two thousand households.

units.zh: 建武末，爲吏部尚書，是時尚書右僕射江祏管朝政，多所進拔，爲士子所歸。
units.en: Late in Jianwu he headed the ministry of personnel; Right Vice Director Jiang Shi then ran court politics, advanced many men, and drew the gentry to him.
units.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was Director of the Ministry of Personnel; at the time Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Shi managed court politics, promoted many men, and was where scholars gathered.

units.zh: 亮以名家子，宋末選尚公主，拜駙馬都尉、秘書郎，累遷桂陽王文學，南郡王友，秘書丞。
units.en: As a son of a great house, at the end of Song he was matched to a princess, made commandant of the horse for the imperial son-in-law and secretary gentleman, and rose through literary scholar to the prince of Guiyang, friend to the prince of Nanjun, and secretary assistant.
units.literal: Liang was a scion of a famous house; at the end of Song he was chosen to marry a princess, made Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-law and Secretary Gentleman, and rose through Literary Scholar to the Prince of Guiyang, Friend to the Prince of Nanjun, and Secretary Assistant.

units.zh: 父攸，給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: His father You was an attendant yellow gate gentleman.
units.literal: His father You was Attendant Yellow Gate Gentleman.

units.zh: 祖偃，宋右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
units.en: His grandfather Yan had been Song right grand master of splendid happiness, opening the government with ritual equal to the three excellencies.
units.literal: His grandfather Yan was Song Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, opening the government with ritual equal to the three excellencies.

units.zh: 遭母憂，居喪盡禮。
units.en: When his mother died he observed mourning in full ritual.
units.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning in full ritual.

units.zh: 齊竟陵王子良開西邸，延才俊以爲士林館，使工圖畫其像，亮亦預焉。
units.en: When Qi's prince of Jingling opened the Western Lodge and gathered worthies for the Scholars' Grove Hall, artisans painted their likenesses—and Liang was among them.
units.literal: Qi Prince of Jingling Zi Liang opened the Western Lodge, gathering talented men for the Scholars' Grove Hall and having artisans paint their portraits—Liang was among them.

units.zh: 時齊明帝作相，聞而嘉之，引爲領軍長史，甚見賞納。
units.en: Qi Emperor Ming was then regent; hearing of him he praised him, made him chief of staff to the guard general, and favored him deeply.
units.literal: At the time Qi Emperor Ming was acting as regent; hearing of this he praised him, brought him in as Chief Staff Officer to the Guard General, and greatly favored and received him.

units.zh: 梁臺建，授侍中、尚書令，固讓不拜，乃爲侍中、中書監，兼尚書令。
units.en: When the Liang regime was set up, he was offered attendant and director of the masters of writing; he refused firmly and was made attendant, director of the secretariat, with the masters of writing added.
units.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was appointed Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; he firmly refused; he was then made Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 天監二年，轉左光祿大夫，侍中、中軍如故。
units.en: In Tianjian's second year he was transferred to left grand master of splendid happiness; attendant and central army were unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Attendant and Central Army unchanged.

units.zh: 詔削爵廢爲庶人。
units.en: An edict stripped his rank and made him a commoner.
units.literal: An edict stripped his rank and made him a commoner.

units.zh: 八年，詔起爲秘書監，俄加通直散騎常侍，數日遷太常卿。
units.en: In the eighth year an edict recalled him as director of the secretariat; soon he was further made regular attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and within days rose to minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: In the eighth year an edict recalled him as Director of the Secretariat; soon he was further made Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and within days was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 九年，轉中書監，加散騎常侍。
units.en: In the ninth year he was transferred to director of the secretariat with additional cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat with additional Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 其年卒。
units.en: That year he died.
units.literal: That year he died.

units.zh: 詔賻錢三萬，布五十匹。
units.en: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for funeral expenses.
units.literal: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for funeral expenses.

units.zh: 始亮未爲吏部郎時，以祏帝之內弟，故深友祏，祏爲之延譽，益爲帝所器重；
units.en: Earlier, before Liang headed personnel, he had been close to Shi—the emperor's brother-in-law—and Shi had praised him, so the throne prized him all the more;
units.literal: At first, before Liang was Director of the Ministry of Personnel, because Shi was the emperor's brother-in-law he befriended him deeply; Shi spread his reputation, so the emperor valued him all the more;

units.zh: 至是與祏昵之如初。
units.en: yet now they were intimate as ever.
units.literal: but now they were as intimate as before.

units.zh: 亮自以身居選部，每持異議。
units.en: Liang, as head of selection, often took the other side.
units.literal: Liang, considering himself head of the selection bureau, often held opposing views.

units.zh: 外若詳審，內無明鑒，其所選用，拘資次而已，當世不謂爲能。
units.en: Outwardly he seemed careful; inwardly he had no clear eye. He chose by seniority alone, and the age did not call him able.
units.literal: Outwardly he seemed careful in review, inwardly he lacked clear judgment; those he selected were bound by seniority alone—the age did not call him capable.

units.zh: 亮反覆不忠，姦賄彰暴，有何可論！
units.en: Liang was faithless and shifting, corruption and bribes openly violent—what is there to discuss!
units.literal: Liang was faithless and shifting, corruption and bribes openly violent—what is there to discuss!

units.zh: 其于取捨，何與三仁之異歟？
units.en: In what he took and rejected, how did he differ from the three worthies?
units.literal: In what he took and rejected, how did he differ from the three worthies?

units.zh: 乃自取廢敗，非不幸也。
units.en: Then he brought ruin on himself—not misfortune.
units.literal: Then he brought ruin on himself—not misfortune.

units.zh: 四年夏，高祖讌於華光殿，謂羣臣曰：「朕日昃聽政，思聞得失。
units.en: In summer of the fourth year Gaozu feasted at Huaguang Hall and told the ministers, "From noon I hear government, wishing to learn gain and loss.
units.literal: In summer of the fourth year Gaozu feasted at Huaguang Hall and said to the assembled ministers: "From noon I hear affairs of state, wishing to learn gain and loss.

units.zh: 義師至新林，內外百僚皆道迎，其未能拔者，亦間路送誠款，亮獨不遣。
units.en: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, officials within and without went out to welcome them; those who could not leave still sent loyalty by back roads—only Liang sent no one.
units.literal: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, officials inside and outside all went out to welcome them; those who could not break away still sent pledges of loyalty by side roads—only Liang sent no one.

units.zh: 元日朝會萬國，亮辭疾不登殿，設饌別省，而語笑自若。
units.en: On New Year's Day the myriad states met in court; Liang pleaded illness, did not mount the hall, dined in a side office, and talked and laughed as if at ease.
units.literal: On New Year's Day the myriad states assembled in court; Liang pleaded illness and did not ascend the hall, set out food in a separate office, yet talked and laughed as if at ease.

units.zh: 數日，詔公卿問訊，亮無疾色，御史中丞樂藹奏大不敬，論棄市刑。
units.en: Days later an edict sent dukes and ministers to inquire; Liang showed no sickness; censor-in-chief Yue Ai memorialized gross disrespect and asked the death penalty in the marketplace.
units.literal: Several days later an edict had the dukes and ministers inquire; Liang showed no sign of illness; Censor-in-Chief Yue Ai memorialized for gross disrespect, penalty of execution in the marketplace.

units.zh: 遷中書侍郎、大司馬從事中郎，出爲衡陽太守。
units.en: He rose to secretariat gentleman and chief staff officer to the grand marshal, then went out as Hengyang governor.
units.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Chief Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, and went out as Governor of Hengyang.

units.zh: 尋拜晉陵太守，在職清公有美政。
units.en: Soon he was Jinling governor—pure in office, with a reputation for good rule.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Jinling; in office he was pure and public-spirited, with fine governance.

units.zh: 及卽位，累遷太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎，詮序著稱，遷侍中。
units.en: When Ming took the throne, Liang rose to crown prince palace attendant and director of the ministry of personnel—his rankings won fame—and then to attendant.
units.literal: When Ming took the throne, he rose through offices to Crown Prince Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel—his evaluations won renown—and was promoted to Attendant.

units.zh: 及祏遇誅，羣小放命，凡所除拜，悉由內寵，亮更弗能止。
units.en: When Shi was killed, petty men had their way; every appointment ran through inner favorites, and Liang could not stop it.
units.literal: When Shi was executed, petty men ran wild—all appointments passed through inner favorites, and Liang could no longer stop them.

units.zh: 旣而東昏肆虐，淫刑已逞，亮傾側取容，竟以免戮。
units.en: Then Eastern Depravity raged and cruel punishments ran their course—Liang bent to please and barely escaped death.
units.literal: Then Eastern Depravity ran rampant and cruel punishments had their day—Liang leaned this way and that to please and escaped death by a hair.

units.zh: 亮出見高祖，高祖曰：「顛而不扶，安用彼相。」
units.en: Liang came out to see Gaozu. Gaozu said, "When the tottering man is not held up, what use is that minister!"
units.literal: Liang came out to see Gaozu; Gaozu said: "When the toppling man is not supported, what use is that minister!"

units.zh: 璽書詰縝曰：「亮少乏才能，無聞時輩，昔經冒入羣英，相與豈薄，晚節諂事江祏，爲吏部，末協附梅蟲兒、茹法珍，遂執昏政。
units.en: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among his peers; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we were not thin with one another; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as director of personnel he finally joined Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and held benighted government.
units.literal: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among contemporaries; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we with one another were not thin; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as Director of Personnel he finally joined with Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and so held benighted government.

units.zh: 亮協固凶黨，作威作福，靡衣玉食，女樂盈房，勢危事逼，自相吞噬。
units.en: Liang joined the vicious faction, made might and made blessing, fine clothes and jade food, female musicians filling the rooms; when peril pressed and business forced, they devoured one another.
units.literal: Liang solidified with the vicious faction, made might and made blessing, fine clothes and jade food, female musicians filling the rooms; when peril pressed and business forced, they devoured one another.

units.zh: 亮因屏居閉掃，不通賓客。
units.en: Liang then lived in seclusion, swept his quarters, and received no guests.
units.literal: Liang then lived in seclusion, swept his quarters, and received no guests.

units.zh: 瑩從弟亮旣當朝，於瑩素雖不善，時欲引與同事。
units.en: Cousin Liang was then in power; though never close to Ying, he now wished to draw him into shared office.
units.literal: Ying's cousin Liang was then in power; though he had never been close to Ying, he now wished to draw him into shared office.

units.zh: 亮之進退，失所據矣。
units.en: In advance and retreat, Liang lost what he should have stood on.
units.literal: In advance and retreat, Liang lost what he should have stood on.

units.zh: 八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，從典援筆擬之，便有佳致。
units.en: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works. Seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush to match it and at once produced something fine.
units.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works; seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush and imitated it, and at once achieved fine effect.

units.zh: 成王不疑周公，孝昭委任霍光，各因其時以成名，大矣哉！
units.en: King Cheng did not doubt the Duke of Zhou; Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang with power. Each, in his own time, achieved renown thereby. How great this was!
units.literal: King Cheng did not doubt the Duke of Zhou; Emperor Zhao the Filial entrusted power to Huo Guang—each in his time achieved renown thereby. How great!

units.zh: 祖孝嗣，太尉、枝江文忠公。
units.en: grandfather Xiaosi, Grand Commandant, Duke of Zhijiang the Cultured and Loyal.
units.literal: grandfather Xiaosi, Grand Commandant, Duke of Zhijiang the Cultured and Loyal.

units.zh: 父緄，侍中、信武將軍。
units.en: father Chun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Trustworthy Martial General.
units.literal: father Chun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Trustworthy Martial General.

units.zh: 乃遣國子博士范雲、舍人裴長穆等使石頭城詣高祖，高祖以稷爲侍中、左衛將軍。
units.en: Then he sent National University erudite Fan Yun, attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to see Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji attendant within and left palace guard general.
units.literal: Then he sent National University Erudite Fan Yun, Attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to present themselves to Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji Attendant Within and Left Palace Guard General.

units.zh: 於是諸侯王及 太尉長安侯臣綰等三百人，與博士稷嗣君叔孫通謹擇良日二月甲午，上尊號。
units.en: So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal, Marquis of Chang'an, Wan, and 300 others, together with the Erudite Lord Jisi, Shusun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.
units.literal: So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal Lord Chang'an Chen Wan and 300 others, together with Erudite Ji, Successor Lord Shu Sun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.

units.zh: 天下既定，命蕭何次律令，韓信申軍法，張蒼定章程，叔孫通制禮儀，陸賈造新語。
units.en: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shusun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.
units.literal: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shu Sun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.

units.zh: 春正月，追尊兄伯號曰武哀侯。
units.en: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.
units.literal: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.

units.zh: 老子曰：「其政察察，其人缺缺。」
units.en: Laozi said, "When government is excessively exacting, the people grow impoverished in spirit."
units.literal: Laozi said: "When government is minutely scrutinizing, the people are deficient and incomplete."

units.zh: 又曰：「法令滋章，盜賊多有。」
units.en: He also said, "When laws and statutes proliferate, thieves and bandits multiply."
units.literal: He also said: "When laws and decrees multiply, robbers and bandits abound."

units.zh: 又嘗詣徵士何胤，時太守衡陽王亦造焉，胤言之於王，王欲見荔，荔辭曰：「未有板刺，無容拜謁。」
units.en: He once visited the recluse He Yin. The Prince of Hengyang, then administrator, also came; Yin spoke of Li to the prince, who wished to see him. Li declined: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."
units.literal: He also once visited the recluse He Yin; at the time the Administrator, the Prince of Hengyang, also came, and Yin spoke of him to the prince; the prince wished to see Li, but Li declined, saying: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."

units.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞
units.en: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
units.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

units.zh: 蔡邕創立此志，馬彪勒成漢典，晉摯虞治禮，亦議五輅制度。
units.en: Cai Yong began this treatise; Ma Biao finished the Han record; under Jin, Zhi Yu curated the rites and debated the five ceremonial chariots as well.
units.literal: Cai Yong founded this treatise; Ma Biao compiled the Han canon; Jin's Zhi Yu curated the rites and likewise debated the system of the Five Regalia Chariots.

units.zh: 與梁人泛言氏族，袁狎曰：「未若我本出自黃帝，姓在十四之限。」
units.en: With the men of Liang he spoke at large on clans; Yuan Xia said, "Still not as good as my house — we issue from the Yellow Emperor and our surname stands within the fourteen."
units.literal: With the men of Liang he spoke at large on clans; Yuan Xia said: "Still not as good as my house — we issue from the Yellow Emperor and our surname stands within the fourteen."

units.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
units.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
units.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

units.zh: 頃之，又副領軍王瑩。
units.en: Soon afterward he again served as deputy to Wang Ying, Commander of the Army.
units.literal: Soon afterward he again served as deputy to Wang Ying, Commander of the Army.

units.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。
units.en: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.
units.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 儉雅欽重昉，以爲當時無輩。
units.en: Jian prized him deeply and said no man of the time matched him.
units.literal: Jian deeply admired Fang and thought there was no equal in the age.

units.zh: 江左初為周顗、蘇峻宅，其後為袁悅宅，又為章武王司馬秀宅，皆以凶終。
units.en: In the early years south of the Yangtze it had been the home of Zhou Yi and Su Jun; later of Yuan Yue, then of Prince Zhangwu Sima Xiu—all met violent ends.
units.literal: In the early years south of the Yangtze it was the residence of Zhou Yi and Su Jun; afterward it was Yuan Yue's residence, then Prince of Zhangwu Sima Xiu's residence—all ended in violent death.

units.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
units.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
units.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.
